The Clockwork Mansion is probably the most innovative level design ive ever seen in a video game.
If you manage to get past the technical issues, or never had them (like me), then I fully recommend this as a continuation to the Dishonored storyline.

Where Dishonored felt like an oil painting with broad strokes of colour and details which are suggested moreso than depicted, Dishonored 2 feels like a series of sculptures with very defined shapes and a hyper-attention to detail.
This carries over to the gameplay. Dishonored's maps felt like a maze, whereas 2' feel like mazes within mazes, backed up with some incredible environmental storytelling and world building which does compensate for Victor Antonov's absence in the art direction.
It's harder and more of a slog than the first and the story does rely on far more contrivances and belief suspension in general, but as someone who found the first far too easy, I'm fine with this.
It's worth paying the price of admission for The Clockwork Mansion alone. Ingenius level design.

So.. I just completed my 6th playthrough of Dishonored 2.
I'm at a point where I know the game so well that I'm beating it about once a day and as of right now my PB time is 1 hours and 43 minutes.
I can't stop playing this game.
One of the things I absolutely love about all the Dishonored games (this one included, of course), is its replayability value. This game, unlike any other I have played, has such an incredible amount of replayability. I've played and beaten the game 6 times now and I could easily go back and play it a 7th.
After this many playthroughs, however, the story has gotten a bit pointless to me and I'm just playing for the gameplay.
The gamplay/combat mechanics are phenominal. There's so many ways to approach a mission and the combat mechanics of the game are some of my favorite.
Speaking again about the story:
It was a good story the first couple times I played through it. Not the best or most compelling story I've ever played, but I liked it. The cutscenes are detailed and well done and the dialogue is really great alongside it. But again.. the story itself isn't fantastic and I've definitely played better. I like the first Dishonored's story a  lot more.
The level design is insane. The maps are massive and there's so many way to do everything and get everywhere. Even on my 4th or 5th playthrough I was discovering new things in the levels.
In its current state, the game runs perfectly for me and I've had no stability problems or any bugs relating to the playability of the game. I've only found one very minor bug while playing and it seems to only come up when I'm speedrunning. On a certain mission (7 I believe.. At Sokolov's mansion), the objective marker is just sitting at some random part of the house, not where the actual objective is. This wasn't much of a problem for me since I knew where to go, but it through me for a loop the first time I stumbled across it. Besides that, I've had no issues with the game at all.
Also.. last thing:
The final "battle" of the game is painfully easy if you know what you're doing. It almost feels unfair for it to be as easy as it is. It's a pain to discover it, but once you do, it makes the "final boss fight" more of a "final boss situation". Anyway.. that's it.
Tbh 11/10. Worth the $40? Oh hell yah.
Go buy it.

After years of war the gods decided they had enough. Removing powerful relics from the hands of the kings they hid them in nearby tower. Anyone that was able to retrieve all relics would once and for all be known as ruler of the known world. Playing the roll of
you set out to take your chances at glory and perhaps peace across the lands.
Gameplay quite similar to Alex the Kidd, which isn't a bad thing. Progress is made by surviving through rooms which contain enemies, puzzles and traps. Not required to kill every enemy and they often respawn if you walk off the screen so technically you would be there for an eternity. Climb the tower further and fight bosses followed by eventually reaching segments that showed a minimap  dictating new zones. New areas held one of the sought after relics that rewarded a new skill or weapon along with changes in visual themes, music and increased overall difficulty.
Decent chiptune soundtrack that could use a little more variation in the loops but it was certainly upbeat and fitting, soundfx took me straight back to yesteryear. Responsive controls though I would suggest a gamepad, will be doing a lot of button tapping using the characters flight skills. Something that tried to set it apart from others in the genre but I personally felt it just made the game easier as it could easily be exploited but likely by design.
Enjoyed my time spent playing thus far and if you enjoy platformers, more-so of the retro variety it's worth checking out. Keep in mind it's not without it's flaws and as it stands @$10 would give it a solid recommend. Would suggest doing further research yourself as always. Cheer folks. :)

Update: Completed Game Review
Ok as this game stands it's good but not great.
First off the gameplay is solid at first, you can fly as long as your meter is full (which can be exploited a bit when you figure out to tap the the jump button). although the hit detection of your sword is a very short range and can get annoying when you move up to enemies to hit them only to get hit yourself. Once you get the dash attack ability (Has you dash in any 4 directions) the game gets an increase in enjoyment when it come to gameplay.
The Item shop, (after you buy the Health increase) is useless. For coins you can get a health refill (Enemies drop health, sooooooooo..... pointless?) an extra life(if you run out you just start back at the last check point you crossed, plus unlimited continues), and for feathers you can get a magic feather (that makes you invulnerable for 15 seconds.......... right after you leave the shop...... wait WHAT? o_O) and a magic potion that refills your hearts once they run out (AKA fairy in a bottle).
Some enemies are programed in Unnecessary Bull♥♥♥♥♥♥that seeps at their very maw........ ok mostly just the flying enemies. The butterfly's do make it difficult in the beginning since the range of your sword is short, and they fly at you in a Boo like fashion from mario bros. Seriously screw butterfly's.
Update: Or maybe I just suck, but you know what, I ABSOLUTELY HATE THOSE DAMN BAT'S THAT FLY FROM THE EDGE OF THE SCREEN IN THE LAST LEVEL. SCREW YOU! YOU F***ING BATS!!!
And that's the only thing I hate from the final level - end anger enduced rant
There are also some area's that will leave you confused, since you have to remeber where you have been and if you go through the wrong door, the door behind you closes and you have to trek through that area all over again just to get back at the area that has multiple doors. Not too much of a problem for me, but for some that could get annoying.
Progession is Great, as you keep going up the game will get progressivly harder, but it seems it's mostly at your pace. Once you learn to deal with some enemies naturally over time, you feel more confident then when it gets to the next area it adds another difficulty. This is pretty solid right here.
Once you get an item that has you charge up your sword....... it takes way to long it seems and just seems to leave you open and is only effective towards one enemy that can be easily avoided.
Update - I was told by the developers that they fixed the sword charging problem, Great job guys. This made me want to use the charge up way more, and once fixed made combat enjoyable again........... except for the bats in the final level.
Update: Bosses are cool looking but can sometimes seem exploitve. I was able to find parts of the bosses where you could find an area to just hang out and spam your attacks. But that could also be a necessity since sometimes the bosses attack paths seemed ridiculous to dodge. Like the Total Biscuit Butterfly Boss battle, that would spawn Little Biscuits to attack you...... I'm still wondering why Total Biscuit was a butterfly. Final Boss was definetly the best part of the boss battles, I won't spoil anything but he's a good fresh challenge.
So overall The game is good, but not something that you should go out of your way to get.
Update: I do love the fact that the developers were able to hear out their audience and fix some problems, and I understand that they cannot go back and make the magic feather of invicibility a more useful item since that might entail changing code which could cause the game to glitch or crash. But thanks again Pixel Barrage for improving after release.
My recommendation:
Update: I still stand by my original conclusion, though Pixel Barrage willing to hear the criticizm and improve upon the game from those remarks, definetly gets a plus in my book.

I tried out The Elder Scrolls Online during the recent free weekend.
It's a massively multiplayer online game that takes place in the continent from all the games combined, though many iconic places you might like to visit are locked behind either one-time or subscription payment--this is in a game you're already paying for!
Combat feels loose and I don't feel engaged by it at all. It features attack animations that give no real sense of impact leaving PVP feeling slow and endless, with both sides constantly regenerating health with skills. For PVE, The Elder Scrolls Online uses a system similar to Skyrim's for the difficulty: scaling enemy levels. This means that you can travel anywhere in the world without fear of running into really powerful enemies, but it also means that you'll have no trouble anywhere in the game world at all, if you're careful.
Elder Scrolls games aren't known for their story, but when you're with friends in a call together, that story becomes completely irrelevant. It's hard to justify sitting around and listening to slow uninspired voice acting for five minutes when you could easily skip it and be told where to go with a waypoint.
In fact, the only quest I enjoyed was one where you aren't given any waypoints! It was a treasure hunt that had us looking around for clues while following hints from a note. This quest had us actually collaborate towards a goal, all on the lookout for the next landmark, instead of lazily following a marker from point A to B.
Freedom to play how you want is heavily restricted to the typical MMO format. When we discovered that the cheapest horse in a stable cost a whopping 10,000 gold, could we afford that? No. Could we steal a horse and run off with one? Also no.
Overall I can't say I enjoyed The Elder Scrolls Online. I put about 8 hours into it during this free weekend and the gameplay never got interesting or engaging. From the combat to the exploring to the dialogue, none of it gripped me.
Maybe a fan of MMO games might find something to like in this, but it's decidedly not Elder Scrolls. I'd compare it to an Elder Scrolls-themed attraction at a theme park. Even if it was free, at over 50GB in file size, is it really worth the space? I'm not convinced.

Not entirely happy but it's moving in the right direction.
It's better than their first attempt, but even the reworked game is still quite buggy, feels incomplete and has poor performance (not really, see Edit).
While they did a good job on the models of armours, ships, town buildings, all towns and locations are exactly the same. You keep visiting the same tavern and keep fighting in the same battlegrounds over and over again, which is very immersion breaking to me. Hope this is expanded upon.
Ship combat still seems too gamey, though it's a bit less clunky than before. Ship boarding action is much better, since not all troops spawn at once, so you get more running around the ship, climbing ropes, etc, which is a lot of fun.
The GUI is same ol' M&B, but when new bits were introduced they don't always work smoothly or are bugged. Renamed ships revert back to their original names everytime you go ashore, scrolling through your troops resets to bottom each time you click, etc.
Your companions tend to just disappear sometimes, without you being told whether they were killed in combat, deserted, were captured or went down with a ship. Quests are just declared failed after you clicked on a couple conversation options without really knowing why. This feels unfinished and unintuitive.
Performance is quite terrible for me. I can run M&B Warband: Viking Conquest on max graphics and have battles with several hundred troops, but can only run Caribbean on the most basic graphic settings and still only get framerate of about 30 (not anymore, see Edit).
I haven't yet given up on this game, because I am desperate for a good pirate game, so I'll keep hoping it improves, but still have to compare this game to the ancient game Pirates of the Caribbean with the New Horizons mod, which captured the same spirit, but just did it a lot more credibly
, particularly the sea combat.
If I gave the original Caribbean! 2/10, because it seemed just too broken, I give Blood&Gold: Caribbean! 5/10 (upped to 6/10 after Edit) and just barely recommend it as it just doesn't deliver the full potential of pirating fun it could.
Edit:
After manually adding the game in the NVidia panel, the performance is ok. 80fps at max graphics. Strange though that this game doesn't recognise the graphics card, while M&B Warband does automatically.
I guess I can bump the score to 6/10 and will likely increase more once they fix the bugs, the gamey feeling of sea combat and other loose ends.

A remake of the Caribbean! A Remade Review.
Blood & Gold Caribbean is an improvement over its original.  Many of the player suggestions have been addressed.  Much of the content, that the developers pulled from the M&B Engine, has been re-introduced.  Below is my Pro's and Con's.  Many pro's represent improvements over the original.
PRO:
-Taverns now feel more connected to the Caribbean, nice immersion
-Classical use of the Battle Interface hot-key commands are well re-implemented
-Re-introduction of the zoomable map
-Quest content expanded in fun, cool, and immersive ways
-Ship-boarding battle is well made
-The plantation combat is a nice addition, with fields that hide soldiers
-Dev provided this remake for free to original game owners, this  healthy show of respect for the player-base is noted, and should be counted
-Devs-Active against bugs! (Less than a week after I posted this review with a bug listed, they fixed it!).
CONS:
-Whoever heard of a pirate ship full of non-combatants! Sailors are pacifists... and fighters are hard to come by... Serious? SERIOUSLY, the division of combatants vs sailors is very wierd and problematic
-Pathfinding is pretty bad. Click on one place and be auto-navigated into an enemy port in the other direction
-Lots of sword-swinging, with no connections (weapon coding or collision animation issues?) Watching mounted-swordsman fight for eternity without severely reduced ability to kill each other is sad
-Ship cannonade, has no aim tool or overlay, and you often can't even see where your firing
-Limited Blackjack Players - "Oh, wait, am I in the wrong crowded tavern? Oh, okay, I'll sail the other side of the Caribbean, there should be one over there... DANGIT, wrong one... ."
-Walking around the town is purely cosmetic...
VERDICT: The game is an improvement over the original, but that does not mean it is ready for play.  With some corrections, I feel this game could easily switch over to a positive review... but with BADLY done cannonades (you can't aim), and swords that frequently don't hit, and pirate crews that are programmed to be non-combatants... HUH?  It would be funny, if it didn't frequently lead to frustrating situations that shouldn't exist.  Maybe get it on sale, and hope the Devs fix these OLD issues.

Developed by an indie studio "Power of 2" and published by "Tripwire Interactive" known for "Red Orchestra" and "Killing Floor", this is a unique RTS of multi-tasking for single player, while you protect your base from lots of troubles, you simultaneously need to get more scores for online competition.
The main mode of the game is Arcade, in which you aim to get high score for the online score board within limited time which can be set to 5, 15, 30, 60 minutes.
You take the role of an overseer for dwarfs who randomly moves towards caves for minerals such as gold or silver and direct them at randomly generated map, the more minerals dwarfs get the higher points for score can be gained.
While some caves contain gold or silver that give point for the score, others contain dooms you must stop to save your dwarfs such as lava or flood or monsters.
Although these troubles can be stopped by putting arrows to direct your dwarfs, each arrow consumes gold which can be gained by getting minerals.
In addition, each dwarf gains experience and levels up so careful plan and management for both resource and units are vital.
With 7 other game mode and 4 difficulty levels and 29 achievements to unlock, this game can be your long time friend for its low price.
Not only simple to play and easy to learn with tutorial but also has its depth which makes the game quite addictive, worth buying if you're ok with fast-paced RTS that will keep you busy during the play.
Play F2P (free to play) version, and buy the full version if you like it, it's just for 2.5$ during 75% off sale!
Purchasing the full version or unlocking an achievement by collecting a cumulative total of 40k gold on the F2P version, unlocks "Dwarfs!? Axe", a two-handed melee weapon for Berserker perk in "Killing Floor".

Shame is a strong word but one with many meanings. When i first started playing TheHunter i was ashamed of myself for playing a subscription based game. I used to swear that i would never do such a thing and that anyone who payed monthly for a game was stupid. Thanks to TH's very reasonable prices for membership i now have an outright different view on paid memberships.
First off i believe that having a paid subscription is a fantastic way for a small developer to make money. It means that instead of having one sole purchase and having to survive on the sales of that item they can rest assured that money will continue to flow steadily as long as they keep player interested.
Another good thing i found with subscription based playing ( this does not count for all games of course) is that the community is fantastic! People who are serious about the game pay the money and are 9 times out of 10 a joy to play with and to talk too. I am happy to say that in my time so far in TH i have made a few new friends.
Of course there are some downsides to this games subscription based business plan and it comes in the way of micro-transactions. This evil beast plagues thousands of games and turns away even more than that in potential members. The game currently offers a premium currency that can only be obtained in 3 ways.
1- Paying real money. Thankfully none of this is needed as you can kill every animal with the gun you get from the cheapest starter bundle which is around £11, It includes 3 months subscription, 2 new weapons and some equipment as well as ammunition.
2 - Earning it through surveys and offers from 3rd parties. This is a devious method as it preys on those who are unaware of internet scams. Although people have been able to make large amounts of premium currency known as EM$ this way, there are many tales of woe in which people feel cheated out of their time and sometimes their money.
3 - Compete in competitions. This is a step in the right direction. Competitions that update constantly that offer prizes for first second and third including EM$ prizes.
I think that TH should have a system by which hunting animals rewards you with a small amount of EM$, this will encourage people to play more and try harder at scoring the bigger game as well as making the idea of having micro transactions a luxury for the lazy.
Now this is the part of the review im sure most people care about what do i actually think of that game. Well im addicted. The thrill i get from hunting down an animals and killing it with a perfectly placed shot to the heart or lungs gives me a true sense of satisfaction that other games simply cannot provide. The slow pacing of the game makes it very tense when sneaking up on an elk or aiming carefully and a bear.
The graphics are astonashing. The engine they have used is brilliantly optimised with my mid to high range pc being able to the play the game on full graphics and 30fps constant. The weather effects are by far the best i have ever seen in a game. Think of a game that had amazing weather effects. They are nothing compared to this game. The sounds are amazing, i love hearing a shot echo as i watch the deer fall to the ground with a loud THUD. and finally i cant have a review without talking about the small details, the animations, the minigame, the detail they put into each animal is just astonishing!
I think that this game has some flaws but honestly this is a game that i think people need to play to believe. SO FAR my GOTY.

This may be one of the worst video games I have played. I have tried to give it time and put time into learning the game but it truly is terrible. I have played a lot of motocross video games, this one is at the very bottom. The only thing I like about this game is the support for real bike brands and real sponsors. As far as for the physics of the game: pure crap. When turning, the rider will just randomly fall off of the bike, if the bike even turns at all. The acceleration will cut out after being in the air from a jump, so hitting a rythem section on a track is impossible. After performing a whip over a jump, the front end of the bike will face downward and the bike will land entirelly on the front wheel with all of the weight of the bike and the rider leaning forward. That is 100% unrealistic and there is no way to lean back or combine with the throttle to get the bike to straighten out to the correct position.

The game is really fun! Physics are actually suprisingly great and when the AI is set to realistic; it gives you a challenge (unlike some other motocross games). The bikes look great and so do the riders. I also really like the replay feature (although the ability to rewind would be nice).
However, the game acts like it's in Beta. There are many crashes and glitches. And the landscape and overall graphics are pretty terrible for a game made in 2014 (other than the bikes and riders as I mentioned before). The bikes also sound like total crap. There are also only 14 tracks, no free roam (which is understandable for MXGP, but there should be more tracks), very restricted customization, lack of various in-game social feed responses, and so forth.
Now it may seem like this game is outweighed with con's from my review, but if you are tolerant enough to look past these faults; it's actually a pretty good game. The gameplay is really great and I like the idea of being in different teams and having different sponsors (although you cannot choose your sponsors). I also really appreciate having actual bikes and not having to pay money for DLC that allows me to ride a Honda or a Yamaha.
Overall, I think this game is worth it for anyone that rides motocross or dirt bikes in real life (or perhaps just really like motocross games). But don't expect a complete game, there is a lot that needs to be fixed/added.

This is a game for motocross fans and riders. It's a lot less arcade like than the MX vs ATV series, with a more realistic feel. The handling is pretty awesome with the dual-stick controls and being able to stick to a rut. There are some hiccups with the physics when you get to the outter edge of the tracks, but for the most part they're spot on. This is easily the most fun motocross game I've played. I loved Reflex, and initially coming to this it seemed slow paced and kinda bland, but after racing half a season and really getting the hang of the physics, I can't play Reflex anymore. It is just far to arcade like for me.
My biggest complaint about this game is the whips and scrubs. There is only one animation for a scrub and you're not able to pull the bike back in mid air. The adds a bit to the realism, but its aggravating that I can't scrub just a little off a smaller double and not worry about not bring it back in time. Also the whip is the same story. One animation and no control over the bike. That's what I do miss about Reflex. You can throw a huge whip or just a little tweak for a landing into a corner.
The sounds and graphics are awesome. The only graphics issue I have is the rider is really rigid while riding. There is no knees bending or arm movement as you ride. Other than that, best graphics for the genre.
Overall 9/10 - wish Milestone(developers of the game) would make an AMA Nationals game. I'd love to race Glen Helen, Southwick, Washougal, ect. with this kind of gameplay!

I have to recommend this game. Here is why:
This game, even with all of its flaws, the stupid AI, the ridiculous wars and awful "politics", is at heart a good total war game. The gameplay is just as fun and diverse as any of the others, and the units are all different. Let me riterate that, EACH FACTION HAS DIFFERENT UNITS. That is a big deal and changes how you build each faction's armies. The problem that quickly arises though, is that you can streamline armies, but you'll never even need close to a full army to take down any faction in the game, as the AI are stupid in battle. If you're rome you almost don't have to even try in battles, because Roman legions are OP to the next degree, so a simple army of 10 or less praetorians will do the job against literally any army. Except maybe elephants. Although that's not a fair comparison. Anyway, the politics sucks and there isn't a family tree but there's more game there than that so don't dwell too long. The units, buildings and different cultures are very historically accurate and fight according to how they would have during that time period, so even as a historic battle simulator it succeeds. A good graphics card and the blood and gore pack make this game beautiful, even with the flying heads and chopped limbs. I recommend this game not because it's perfect, but just because it is entertaining. I've played many a campaign, and am looking to play many more in this installment and the next to come. In conclusion: Graphics: V good at medium or above. Gameplay: Often fantastic, especially during tense city sieges and amphibious landings, but will fall short during regular 2D battles as the AI don't put up a fight. Politics: YAWN move along it sucks accept it just ignore it and you can forget it's even there. 7.5/10 Entertaining, but not as in depth as some of the other previous installments. Dark Souls II is an excellent game from a gameplay standpoint. If you like mature, western themed fantasy games, this game is for you. The combat is hard at first, but if you persevere and play smart, the combat is rewarding.
That said, the lore and overall feel of the game is not as strong as Demon Souls or Dark Souls. However, Dark Souls II has the best combat, especially for newbies of the Dark Souls series.
This game is for those that are fans of the following:
The Witcher, The Witcher 2, Skyrim, Oblivion, Risen, and potentially Dragon Age
This game is ot for those who do not like:
Dying, non-casual combat/gameplay, abstract story, non-linear story
Overall, Dark Souls II is a great game.  If I had to attach a rating, it would be a 8.5/10, with Dark Souls I being a 9.5/10. Dark Souls II is a strong sequel, mainly in its refined gameplay, but the feel of the world is a bit lacking. Almost like an MMO where you are given the "tourism" treatment (ie: see this Fire land, see this Snow land, see this Underground land).

I first heard about this game at work in 2014. My coworkers had all stopped playing LoL to try the Smite Beta. I joined them, buying the Ultimate God pack, and now that the game has made it three seasons, I cannot be more satisfied.
While a Moba like league of legends, the combat is reminiscent of classic MMOs like WoW. Auto-attacks are like dumbed-down fps combat because there is no vertical aiming plane. The third-person perspective makes jungling EXTREMELY satisfying because you can sneak up on people while their back is turned. The support meta also dictates the support be like a secondary jungler who roams away from his marksmen to gank mid from time to time. While my main game will always be League of Legends, Smite does an excellent job in making up for many of leagues flaws (more variety in game modes, more satisfying/impactful support meta, guilds that bring players together as comrades,  and no point-and-click skill shots.) Smite is my secondary multi-player.
As far as flaws go, most mobas suffer from imbalance ESPECIALLY at low elo where players dont know how to deal with a particular god. For example, artemis on joust is pretty broken. I have an 80% win-rate with her. But I'm pretty sure if I got to higher elos I would be shut down. Every moba has equivalent carries that few players know how to deal with, and in league, tryndamere and nasus are famous to-gold carries as well.
Finally, I wish smite had a larger player-base. Their's can't compare Dota 2 or LoL. The community's esport scene is in the shadow of league's and dota's as well. As a result, there are few online resources past beginner knowledge to improve your play. While this makes the game feel more casual and less competitive/ over-analytical, I do wish there was a greater focus on creating learning resources of higher tiers. Websites like na.op.gg and probuilds are not up for this game.
Lastly movement is keybound to ASWD and spells to 1 2 3 4, and you move the camera with the mouse. My hands are small and those numbers are difficult to reach. Luckily i have a moba mouse, which has numbers 1-6 on the side of my mouse :3

I would have loved to have been an engineer. Wait, let me qualify that statement. I have never wanted to be an engineer. I would have loved to have been an astronaut. No...wait. I don’t do well in confined spaces. I’m not claustrophobic, just a bit fat. However these two personal failings have not stopped me playing or enjoying Factorio.
It’s a game where you start from scratch and have to build up a production line, making futuristic widgets to achieve the game’s goals. You have to exploit resources and then find a way of getting them to where they need to be so that you can build what you need. You start off with some pretty basic tools, including a trusty pickaxe, to help you hack your way around a pristine landscape and research your way to more sophisticated means of utterly ruining a planet in the name of making stuff. There are bugs that try to stop you, but these can be dispatched in a number of ways. I enjoy running them over with trains but then I enjoy running a lot of stuff over with trains.
Factorio is mainly sandbox with a few scenarios thrown in. The outcomes may be different but the way in which you have to achieve them is basically the same. You set up a resource gathering operation and factory units of greater and greater complexity. And that’s the fun part. You need to experiment and refine and learn from your mistakes. It’s a big logic puzzle but it’s pretty forgiving due to the size of the maps and the amount of resources, which can be configured for more of a challenge. I like this game. It satisfies my need to organise and regulate. If my life contained more conveyor belts I think I would be well on my way to happiness. The only thing that’s missing is the Looney Tunes Factory Theme but you can always have that looping away in the background. Be warned though, you will lose hours to this.

I think this could be the best game I've ever played. And I have played _a lot_ of games. It combines many familiar elements (Terraria, Infinifactory/Spacechem, Alpha Centauri and Starcraft come to mind) but manages to create something original, rich and unique, while keeping everything balanced and, well, criminally fun. I mean, yesterday, I noticed that I had an opened bottle of good lager on the table beside me that I had completely ignored for three solid hours while playing. Not a single sip taken. Now that's intensity.
It's currently early access, but it's very polished and well balanced already. The UI could be improved a little and stuff, but the complaints are quite trivial. I'm just constantly blown away by the sheer goodness of this thing. The current 99% positive reviews is justified in my books.
10/10 very recommend.
Edit: after around 50 hours of intense playing, it began to lose its grasp. It seemed to me that after I had unlocked most of the interesting research projects, there was just not a good enough reason for me to expand my production.
I think that the game would benefit immensely from heartier late game content. My two cents: larger, well-fortified alien colonies in addition to the generic nests and more variety to alien races. I'm thinking in the lines of slowly moving sandworms, ethereal-kind of master race aliens and other scary baddies. And of course to keep things in balance, more military stuff. Long-range ballistic nukes? A jet pack?  Programmable robot armies that automatically mow down those nests? A psi-weapon that causes the buggers to attack their comrades? Invisibility cloak for me to creep into a nest and then roboport-build a turret base right into their backyard and then uncloak and unholster my flame thrower and... well... you know what I mean. Late-game stuff.
But the bottom line is, those 50 hours still made for the best gaming I've had in a long, so I can still strongly recommend this title. It's already a must-buy for a building game fan. I'll start another game after a couple of updates. Thumbs up for creating this masterpiece, devs!

One of the best shooters I've ever played. Can be frustrating due to poor translation and a confusing system of timed side-quests which automatically assign and fail regularly. Learning to ignore these is a leap of faith necessary to enjoy the game.
Once you're past its failings, STALKER is pure and often terrifying fun. Lots of space to roam, a solid item system, believable and intricate interiors. Friendly wanderers, roaming bandits; real choice in weapons & armor rather than your usual planned-out, linear upgrades.
For the frustrated, there are mods out there which fix the translation, alter NPC behavior, permit equipment repair, and so on. If you forgo these, be advised that the first two areas are extremely difficult due to your weak equipment, so avoiding combat there is usually the smart move. There will be plenty of time for payback later.
All in all, a flawed but irreplaceable classic which is not for everyone, but which everyone should try.

Borderlands 2 is one of my favorite games of all time and my favorite co-op shooter. However i will give the fairest review to this game, so ill exclude my bias opinions.

Artstyle/graphics
If you have seen gameplay/pictures of the borderland games, you will notice the unique artstyle to the game. This is cel shaded-style. This gives the game a more unique feel and it also suits the gamestyle, as its a not so serious game.

GAMEPLAY
The gameplay is excellent.I don't want to get into detail with the story, just to evade accidental spoilers, but you don't have to play the other borderlands to understand the story, the story is explained throughout the game, the story is  intriguing and very FUN! The rng system allows for TONS of weapons to be looted by you. According to Gearbox Software, there are over 17,750,000 different variations of weapons in Borderlands 2. Borderlands 2 uses a procedural process to generate its various guns in certain classes, such as handguns, shotguns, assault rifles, sniper rifles, and more, but with many variations of firing speed, reload speed, damage type and more. This means every gun is unique. However as you level up you will see that less guns become as valuable to use as they are outdamaged by many weapons. *cough* unkempt Harold *cough* This is because the game gets alot harder once you've beaten it. There is a mode called true vault hunter mode which includes the same story but with higher level and stronger enemies, but this allows you to progress your character more, allowing you to level up more and find better weapons. To level past 50 you will have to purchase some dlc, however it is not needed to enjoy the game.

I need to make it clear that I played this game with the Mechromancer.
I tried the other classes, but they lacked the charm and fun of the previous game. The Gunzerker was the most interesting but the others were pale compared to Borderlands 1.
The plot is much better this time around, though, and the environments much more varied. No longer do you spend countless hours wandering the same "desert junk yard" which mysteriously has occasional swamps. The huge variety of environments, enemies, and improved music all make for the game to be an over all more enjoyable experience. I rarely got bored with the sameness of anything as I did with the previous game.
The DLC are particularly interesting, and again, I found the arena (or arenas now) to be one of the more enjoyable aspects of the game.
The game tries to sell itself on replayability, like the past one did, but this isn't a feature which particularly interested me. Once I played through all of the content once, I wasn't too keen on doing it all over again just for "better guns." So if you're not big on that stuff either, I can assure you that the game does not rely on replaying content to be fun, like other games (such as Dragonbal Xenoverse) do. You don't have to do anything over and over again.
The villains are hit and miss, but the main badguy, Jack is extremely memorable. He is a very well written sociopath, and it takes you a while to realize exactly what he is because he is that manipulative with his words. Unlike the last game though, the final battle is not difficult in any way, so it's a good thing that the story and previous challenges were fulfilling. The ending is easily much more satisfying than the last game's, which angered more than a few people. That ending is explained and I can say I did genuinely enjoy playing this game with the Mechromancer.
The game does get harder with multiple people playing, and I reccomend this. It gets pretty chaotic and is a ton of fun.
I'd give this am 8.5 or maybe a 9 out of 10.

Note off the bat, this review pertains only to the single player mode and the technical side of CoD: AW.
That said, I have to put my foot down and slam my head against my desk until their is a fine indent of cranium to truly express my frustration in how badly optimized this game is for PC. I refuse to play it again for the simple fact that is crashed well over a couple dozen times during the single player campaign, performance was ridiculous where for what strethes of game play I could get through without a sudden crash to desktop, the game would shutter between running smooth as a babies bum, freshly wiped and powdered; to staggering my frames as if I'd decided to take 1990's astrovan and decide to drive across Omaha Beach during the Invasion of Normandy. I merely finished the single player just because I wanted to be over and done with it and delete this game from my computer and have a young and old religious wiseman from every major religion bless the contents of my rig before I throw it out the window because it's combusted into flames and is signaling Cthulu or some space devil to come and stamp out my existence from history.
That's how I feel about this games performance.
As for the story, nothing of interest to see here. Not that I remember it fondly between technical issues and having memory lapses as I felt I'd already played this game before five or six times. Kevin Spacey being some kind of selling point, quick time events which cause heart palpitations and story cliches which must have been scraped from the bottom of the bucket. You have some neat set pieces here and there, but nothing particularly memorable. Even the use of bionics and such comes across as stale. The ability to choose different abilities at the start of each mission is nothing but a red harring as you'll pretty much have to go with what the game gives you. Cool gadgets you see only once and other mechanics in the game which are either severely underused or pushed into your face with the force of a super nova occuring not less than two light years away from the planet.
Overall, I just didn't have fun with this game. Almost every other game in my Steam and Origin libraries runs just fine, only a few having some special issues which can be solved or the game is simply so old it has trouble running on modern computers. Now I have tried a few different things between overclocking my cpu or gpu or not in hopes of stability. I've lowered graphics down to barely acceptable levels, verified game files, so on an so forth. Advanced Warfare has no excuse to have been ported so badly, so please, I beg you from the bottom of my heart, don't buy this game. Go play any other Call of Duty if you want to have a fun time shooting baddies without having to use to much brain power. Why? It's fun. Advanced Warfare on the other hand even destroyed that inane guilty pleasure.

I have to recommend this game. Here is why:
This game, even with all of its flaws, the stupid AI, the ridiculous wars and awful "politics", is at heart a good total war game. The gameplay is just as fun and diverse as any of the others, and the units are all different. Let me riterate that, EACH FACTION HAS DIFFERENT UNITS. That is a big deal and changes how you build each faction's armies. The problem that quickly arises though, is that you can streamline armies, but you'll never even need close to a full army to take down any faction in the game, as the AI are stupid in battle. If you're rome you almost don't have to even try in battles, because Roman legions are OP to the next degree, so a simple army of 10 or less praetorians will do the job against literally any army. Except maybe elephants. Although that's not a fair comparison. Anyway, the politics sucks and there isn't a family tree but there's more game there than that so don't dwell too long. The units, buildings and different cultures are very historically accurate and fight according to how they would have during that time period, so even as a historic battle simulator it succeeds. A good graphics card and the blood and gore pack make this game beautiful, even with the flying heads and chopped limbs. I recommend this game not because it's perfect, but just because it is entertaining. I've played many a campaign, and am looking to play many more in this installment and the next to come. In conclusion: Graphics: V good at medium or above. Gameplay: Often fantastic, especially during tense city sieges and amphibious landings, but will fall short during regular 2D battles as the AI don't put up a fight. Politics: YAWN move along it sucks accept it just ignore it and you can forget it's even there. 7.5/10 Entertaining, but not as in depth as some of the other previous installments. Worth getting on sale

This game is a drug. It starts with you mining by hand. First some stone, then coal, copper and finally iron. then you can build a burner mining drill and a stone furnace, Then you think "hey i can make those automated by adding some inserters in the right places" but now you need a steam engine to get things really working.
Then you remember your surroundings, your mind turns off auto drive and turns back to manual. You find yourself looking down upon an automated machine the size of a province and at first you wonder how someone could make such a thing.
And then it hits you, every detail, every movement. You know what each inch of your assembly line is for. You know which assembling machines produce iron gear wheels and you know exactly how long the conveyor belt is before they are turned into inserters. This is your work, your mind, every single piece of it.
You will be ashamed with how much time you spent on this.
You will be disgusted with how much time you spent on this.
You will consider how much of your life you are missing because of this.
You will realize that if you rearanged your conveyor belts you could produce your green sience 15% faster.
Kiss the next week of your life goodbye.

Since this game is kind of special for me, its time to do an appropriate review of it.
What i like so much about this game is simply cause of the abondance of content and things to do, loot to find and enemies to kill/get killed by. Doesnt it feel good to progress and then complete a game that isnt holding your hand for once? I dont miss the objective marker and quest description of other games when i was just exploring and having fun without having a constant mission reminder harassing me to ''go there'' and ''kill this enemy and get this specific item back to the guy''. And for those who dont want to buy this cause ''omg its too hard'', as long as you learn the combat mechanic and dont be careless, i dont see how you wont get through the game.
This game Take about 40-60 hours to complete on your first playthrough, with each consecutive new game increasing in difficulty for a decent replayability. Simply put, this is best game of 2014 so far.  In a year filled with several disppointing releases, Dark Souls II was a bright spot.   It isn't quite as good as the first game, but that's fine.  It's still a great game.  It gets so many things right that so many other games get wrong.   I've grown tired and bored of AAA titles you can beat in less than 15 hours and offer no significant challenge.   Most of them look gorgeous and have a solid story.  Don't get me wrong, there's a time and a place for that, but not when the market is saturated with titles like that.  Dark Souls II brings back that old school feeling to gaming, back when it was a niche market and you could make a hard game, one where not everyone was going to win and finish (at least not without a lot of effort).  In some games, even if you die your progress is saved a few moments before.  I sometimes think "Why even bother with the death then, since it doesn't mean anything."
Dark Souls II makes every fight count.  The stakes are high enough that you have to .   It's a breath of fresh air in an era where so many games are scared to let someone fail, to make mistakes and actually face consequences for them.  The people who say the game is too hard just don't get it.
Also, the way they handle multiplayer is excellent.   Instead of some tacked on multiplayer deathmatch mode, multiplayer is woven into the fabric of the regular game in a novel way.   I wish they would have done less to discourage invasion by other players (cracked red eye and blue eye orbs are relatively hard to come by, especially early on), but I can see constant invasions would alienate a lot of other players.   Still, I was excited ever single time I got summoned to the Bell Tower to take out an intruder.
It's not without its flaws though.  Some of the bosses this time around were too easy.   I'm looking at you Nashandra.  For the last boss of the game, she should have been way harder than that.   The hitboxing can be janky at times too, especially in multiplayer.   You can learn to play around this, but it's frustrating to be cleary out of range and still take damage from an attack.   Those are really the only two complaints I have.  With the DLC they are putting the mercilessly hard bosses back in the game, so even that is being taken care of.   I spent hours trying to beat the Fume Knight.   I kept thinking "This is what Nashandra should have been.  This is like Gwyn, Lord of Cinder."

What a phenomenal example of what great gameplay and worthwhile DLC can be.  I played this back when it first released, and only picked up the Mechromancer DLC.  Put about 170 hours into it, and was thoroughly satisfied with the money I'd put into it.  Several years later, the GOTY edition went on sale for $10, and included almost all of the DLC I hadn't experienced.  Scooped it up and hopped back in, and I have to say it was absolutely worth every penny all over again.
If you somehow haven't played this yet, and are perhaps on the fence between this and the "Pre-Sequel", go for this one as a GOTY package.  You'll have one more DLC to optionally buy that increases your max level to 72 and unlocks a few other challenges, and I have to say that too is worth it.  The skins, however, I feel are mostly worthless, as you almost never see your character, except while in menu screens.  They do show a bit of flair if you're playing with friends.
Overall, it's a delightful experience with quite a bit of (self-aware and crass) humor.  If you enjoy shooters with a fairly open-world feel and Diablo-style loot mechanics (there are farm-able items that are very much worth the effort when you get to end-game), then absolutely go for it.  I've played through this game multiple times with most of the characters, and it's been a blast every time.  The game's cell-shaded graphics even hold up pleasingly well, and it seems to run quite well on most systems.

I've been playing Total War since 2002 when Medieval came out and have owned all of them at some point.  I waited until recently to purchase as friends who bought at release hated it. The AI cleverly opens it's gates if you bombard with artillery ( I have got an AI mod so may not on vanilla ) so you can't destroy it.  They don't actually shut they gate again after you run out of ammo but you can't charge any units through as there is just a red line in the doorway stopping you.  I've just added a seige ram mod as they are not standard in the game like the first Rome for some reason to see if that sorts it when I use instead of artillary. These days with the modding community games are about customising them to your preferences with the original release being more of a base to start from.  That said I would be much more likley to purchase near release and pay more for them ( I only paid £7.50 on a steam deal ) if they were at leat working right from the box.

Seeing as it's often misunderstood by the newcomers I'll state it right here :
"B&G Caribbean!" is a FREE EXPANSION to the original "Caribbean!"
There are COMPLETELY NO FEES, OR PAYMENTS REQUIRED for the owners of the game.
After not-so-warmly welcomed release of Caribbean! The developers of SnowBird put a lot of effort
to completely revamp the game and provide players with greatly enchanced experienced. Different than what players had expeirienced so far on this engine. Did they succed in that? Yes they did!
(It's still the same game, but honestly there are some things I didn't even have idea they are possible on this engine. Mainly the missions.)
At the very first glance, player may think to himself that not that much has changed, but do not let that fool you. In just a couple of minutes you are guaranteed to get amazed with creativity and new possibilities.
My personal number one, would be the new taverns, where not only you can play BlackJack, or hit another guest with a chair, but also take on the... less legal missions. And the variety of these... is just amazing.
While these I'll call them mini-missions are usually very hard, they are also just so much fun, you get to escort an individual and protect him form assasin attacks, or try and seize the control of a ship stationed in the docks, there are hold out missions, and even sabotage ones. With the time I spent in the game so far, I haven't had time to get bored with these.
There are also various interesting missions from the governors from other countires.
Now I'd also like to talk about the capture system. Most likely most people assumed that new system for being captured is something they won't be using all that often, since they instantly re-load the game if they are defeated. But honestly, on the low levels if player is not careful it's quite easy to end up as a slave and the trasition is so fluent there is no time to load the game. Sure you can still do that a moment later, but honesetly I myslef haven't done so once. Getting ready for your uprising and finally trying to break out free is a lot of fun.
However, you should remember that your goal is to escape throm the plantation or mine, not to kill all the guards. Even with huge uprising like 80 out of 107 prisoners, the plantation garrison is just very strong. So do not waste your chance trying to kill all of them - run for your life.
The Sea battles and feet management have been changesd slightly too. 1) You can now own several fleets stationed in different Bays or ports.
Your ships not being currently used by a character can be always used to form a convoy and sell goods. Be wary of the pirates though! The Sea battles themselvs are now happening in a bit faster pace, and ships are slightly more responsive... Personally I liked it like it was, but this was popular complaint, so it was adressed. There is also a new mechanic, that allows to destroy cannon or cannons of enemy ship. The same may happen to you though!
Last thing I will take note of, is there are a couple of new character skills, one allowing player to cheat in Blackjack more efficently, the other one allows player army to use more cannons, and makes canoneers more efficient. Ah right, about the cannons, they play a lot bigger role in
sieges now, along with destructible defense structures.
There are many more new features, that I am planning on writing about, but I will add these later on, since I want to post this review as quickly as possible :P
For the Multiplayer gamemode, at this stage it's only a very early beta, so I will not include it in the review just yet. This aspect of the game will be updated according to player needs / requests, but it will take some more time. At the very moment it's only a bare skeleton. Hoping an update will come soon.
At this point I'm sure no one needs further proofs that developers will deliver on their promises if given enough time.

Honestly, it is rather sad that the best Space RTS game made in the 16 years since Homeworld 1 came out in 1999 happens to be this, the remastered version of that same game. If you are a fan of the genre you won't regret buying this, especially since you can replace the generic and rather ugly units in the game with those of your Sci-fi of choice (Star Trek, Star Wars, Battlestar, Halo, etc) for the ultimate experience.

Why, Gearbox?  Why couldn't you have either just cleaned it up, or given it the love it needed?  This frankenstein's monster of a game is offensively disrespectful to your history and your legends.
The upgraded graphics break the game - many people report a 'general failure' any time they try to load, and disabling many graphical features seems to be the only (unreliable) fix.  Formations and simulated projectile bullets are gone, both foundational mechanics.
Whereas HW1 achieved it's balance by making ships and weapons actually function according to their role, HWC:RM achieves its balance via HW2's rock/paper/scissors balance, by arbitrarily weighting certain ships to function less effectively against ships they aren't meant to be useful against. Actual simulated projectiles and formations were never made to function in HWC:RM.
If they had just upgraded textures and models and called it a day, they would have shown this game more respect.  Instead, they crammed it into an engine it wasn't meant for, ignored everything that became broken because that new engine doesn't support foundational game mechanics, and released it with numerous game-breaking bugs that after almost two years they never bothered to patch, despite a number of balance patches.

An amazing game about automation and managing the supply logistics of a futuristic factory on a hostile alien world. The true joy of this game is the sense of accomplishment one gets from setting up machines to build an otherwise complicated item in bulk, often in hundreds and thousands of units. Each step up is practically logarithmic, requiring many resources that get refined and folded back into themselves. It's strange to say, but the closest feeling to pulling this off is when you finally kill a difficult boss in Dark Souls- you are faced with a challenge that seems insurmountable until you chip away at it and figure out the quirks by trial and error, even if it isn't obvious at first.
You will go through 3 phases of thinking with each new challenge: What do I have to do, How do I do it, and How do I do it more better? Factorio will draw you in for hours as you make strides in automation and fix any shortages that crop up from your increased production.
The best TL;DR comes from a Reddit comment: "I have to expand my base to meet the needs of expanding my base".

Factorio is a wonderful game.  Most games I move on once I've "figured them out", often before fully completing them.  This one has held my attention for much much longer.  Why?
1) It's about building!
2) It's about automating!
Those two are usually enough to get going, but not to stay so long :)
What keeps it going is
1) The right amount of flexilbiity that your factory never turns out the same, even if you use similar patterns.
2) There are many ways to play the game
3) Really good mod community - Want nuclear reactors?  Harder enemies?  Scarier nights?  Planes?  Different kinds of ores?  Or just a new paint job for your train?  All there.
4) Devs that care about quality - fix bugs before features.  The game has always been solidly playable for me as long as I have had it.
5) Devs that think deeply and communicate often - it is good to see some computer science happening back there to make it efficient and work properly across different platforms.  I like computer science.
Never before has a game made me want to quit what I am doing and make my own game.  Or join theirs :-)

A belated review, because I like to wait for all patches and bugfixes to drop, based on a complete playthrough.
Dishonored 2 is a beautiful looking and sounding game with amazing level design, improved gameplay building on Dishonored 1, bad writing and some questionable voice acting choices.
There is a lot to like. The level design is excellent, providing many paths through levels. This is supported with open gameplay offering a lot of approaches to any given situation - whether quick, thorough, methodical, stealthy, or being the ultimate vengeful killing machine; or switching between them as one likes. The graphics are beautiful, sounds provide well-working audio clues.
Further below are spoilers.
Where the game fails is in my opinion its writing. The writing is shallow, devoid of nuance, black and white and contains a lot of current social justice themes in a preachy way. Unlike in Dishonored 1, very little is left to one's imagination. What was once just an insinuation for the attentive player, is now said explicitly and repeated throughout the game (as the most obvious example the identity of the heart). Emily is a very promising character with no development whatsoever aside from "now I have seen the injustices I used to ignore and I will try to be better". Delilah's motivation as the wronged ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ child doesn't work believably. The game can't decide whether she is cruel and sadistic (she is) or if she deserves our pity for being the poor ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ child (she does, at least according to the game). The same goes for another bad actor - the serial killer Hypatia. She suffers from a split personality and just like other bad women in the game is presented just as a victim of circumstances. What's more - after she (her sane part) learns about the killing, she has almost no reaction to it! The shallowness of the writing can be seen very well on Anton Sokolov. He lost all his nuance from the previous game. The writers imbued him with a new, interesting topic - old age. But all he does with it is moan how he aches and how he looks forward to dying.
There is also an unpleasant streak of current social justice themes that don't belong in the world and that weren't there in the first game. Emily is a bisexual, at least in English (in German, French and other languages with declined verbs the translators decided to make her a heterosexual). A rich silver baron loves the workers' union in his mines, fulfills their every request (thus precluding their raison d'etre at all) and at your last meeting demands that you strive to create "a more inclusive" society.
With Arkane being located in the USA and with Harvey Smith publicly praising Anita Sarkeesian, I guess this change of tone was inevitable. It makes me fear for their next projects. Arkane has some of the best level and gameplay designers in the world today, but I hope they won't hide their work behind preachy, shallow writing.
And last but not least among my criticism: The voice actors are much blander than in the first game. I loved the English voice acting of Piero Joplin and The Outsider. There is now no one as good as Joplin and The Outsider changed from melancholic to just a normal voice actor.
All in all Dishonored 2 is a good game with rich gameplay, amazing level design and some frustrating writing and voice acting. I recommend the game.

Beautiful update of one of the best RTS games I've ever played. Unfortunately, under the hood lie some significant issues. In the original version of HW 1 it didn't rely on random number generation for weapons to hit their targets(and how much damage dealt), if your round visibly hit the enemy it did the appropriate damage. This means the pathfinding and formation AI were critical, especially for your smaller craft. The update didn't get this right and makes half to a third of your combat units useless. (Case in point, 20 bombers could wreck a group of 8 capital ships. I just had 70 shredded without knocking out a single one). Additionally, the resource collectors need to get reassigned repeatedly if you want to pick up everything in a map, and salvage/repair vessels used to be smart enough to figure out what needed to be done if you selected an area, but now you need to micromanage them, adding tedium. I love this game, art direction, soundtrack, story, etc with all my heart and it hurts to see part of what made the original a revelation in the genre not work properly. Pick it up and demand the developers update until it's the game it should be.

I love Homeworld. I read about, and waited for the original. I managed to get into the original beta (I have the CD framed). I played this game for hours and days on end. I was depressed when it turned out that the remote turrets were op in mass, and a created nearly unbeatable playing strategy. I felt like a hero when I found a way to beat it. I endured many losses, and more victories playing friends online. I once managed to steal an entire enemy players capital ship fleet with my own fleet of salvage corvettes and a cloaking frigate. THIS, This was Homeworld. Strategy, intuitive interface, as may ships as your computer could handle, and ships that did what you told them.

Preface: I come from a deep motocross background
After playing this game for a few days, I can, without a doubt, say that this game is the most realistic motocross game out right now.  Unfortunately the bar isn't set very high, considering the only competition to this game is previous titles from the same developer.
Despite how realistic everyone says the rider physics are, how authentic everyone says the track and bike physics are, and despite the fact that they (the devs) call this game a "simulator" in the opening credits, the idea that this game represents a realistic take on motocross is laughable at it's very best.
Every single AI rider will attempt to scrub seemingly every small bump they ride up to, no matter how much time they lose wobbling off a small jump that didn't require them to scrub any speed at all.  If you hit a rider, expect him to stay upright while you go flying.  If another rider hits you, expect him to stay upright while you go flying.  If you hit the yellow dirt, rather than the brown dirt, expect to get thrown off your bike.  How depends on the angle you approach the white dirt at speed.  But as soon as you hit it, you either start floating while flailing your arms while your bike sinks into the ground, or you literally fall right through the bike and start ragdolling all over the place.  It's just infuriatingly stupid.
The very last race I ran, a rider came down on top of my bike and literally rode a third of a lap on top of my helmet.  When he finally dismounted... I crashed.  He didn't.  I mean, FFS?
Also, "career mode" is nothing more than a continuous championship mode with the choice of bike livery between seasons.  There's no depth or fun.  You don't feel like you're building or contributing to anything.  You just simply race, go back to the silly appartment, rinse and repeat.  Oh, but you can pick your helmet (I'm rolling my eyes).
Want to know what pisses me off even more?  The fact that they force you to use mouse and keyboard in menus unless you want to guess which buttons do what.  For a game that is a true to life ♥♥♥♥♥♥ console port, you'd think they'd at least have some decent controller setup and support.
And multiplayer... ♥♥♥♥ing multiplayer.  I can't comment on it because it just plain doesn't work.  I've created an account, I've activated it via email, and even visted their website using it.  But any time I click on multiplayer, it tells me I need an activated account to play.
The one redeaming quality this game has is that it's track deformation isn't matched in any game, any genre, anywhere.  (And... I take this back.  SpinTires puts it to absolute shame.  VBS2.5 also does better, though I couldn't call it a game.)  There are more fun racing games.  There are more fun motocross games, for that matter.  There are certainly more realistic racing games, even with bikes, despite the unfortunate fact that there are no MX game competitors.
Do I reccomend this game?  Only if you REALLY REALLY REALLY need to ride a dirt bike in a game.  Otherwise, spend your money on something less half-baked.
PS: the graphics don't look nearly as good as the screenies.  The graphics suck.  Expect terrain LOD popping at all times as well.

If you're looking for the definitive "Souls" experience, Dark Souls nailed it in 2011. This game feels more like fan-service, a supplement to a growing franchise.
Dark Souls 2 feels like a video game, and nothing more. While I enjoyed this installment quite a bit, I found myself put off by the lack of imagination in the art direction and level design. Even as the first game relentlessly punished you, it did so within fantastic worlds that felt like they were meticulously crafted. The nooks and crannies of levels like Darkroot Garden and Anor Londo felt as though they were deftly crafted and cleverly hidden. The atmosphere was never broken. This is just a personal opinion, but this game feels laden with common, cliched fantasy themes of knights, dragons, the undead and so on without much of the narrative embellishment that would make their appearance more significant than what pop culture would have you believe. The creative spark is evidently absent here, and unfortunately a somewhat dwarfed dragon king man-thing with hulking man-arms doesn't strike me as creative. However, as harsh as I can make my criticism on this point, I firmly believe that creativity was not From's main goal with this game.
It seems Dark Souls 2 wants to live up to the legacy of its predecessors by ensuring high difficulty. But man, it is absolutely fixated on it. The rolling animation and hitboxes have been tweaked to ensure your strafing won't always avail you, you open a door and can almost always anticipate when you're about to take on a horde of a bunch of guys that looks similar to the bunch of guys you've been killing for the past five minutes. And this is where I take issue. Dark Souls destroyed me time and time again, but I never felt it was out to get me. This game pursues you relentlessly. Enemies (probably in armor and humanoid, same old boring stuff) will constantly double up on you and destroy the harmonic one-at-a-time rhythm that the game trains you to adopt early on. Dark Souls 2 was never about getting lost in the atmosphere, but about rising to the challenge that the developer wanted me to be impressed by.
Only I wasn't. In Dark Souls, even the worst deaths taught me how to elude such a fate the next time, and despite how frustrated I may get, I couldn't fault the game. With this installment however, I knew cheap tactics when I saw them. Five hollow soldiers attacking me at once is certainly more grueling than just one, but this artificially ramps up the difficulty in a way I can't respect. The kicker is that despite all the times that Dark Souls 2 tries this, the first game feels more difficult. Enemies were varied and complex and demanded patience and skill, whereas here you can clearly cheese most of the game with ranged attacks.
There are even boss fights where the difficulty feels unnecessarily steep simply because it's two bosses instead of one. I get the idea of how it makes the fight more difficult, but certainly not more interesting. One particularly amorous duo from Dark Souls' mid-game was painfully difficult because you were pitted against two foes with dynamically different fighting strategies. Same basic idea, just as punishing, but much more interesting. Divide and conquer is always the cardinal rule to taking out foes, and that particular boss fight demanded that you work out a rhythm based on the disparity in agility of your foes. Tough as nails, but the strategy always became apparent if you were patient and observed. Dark Souls 2 does not follow suit, and these duo (and trio) encounters routinely demanded that I simply dodge for a few minutes and attack when lady luck gives me an opening. There is no concrete strategy, and your patience goes entirely unrewarded most of the time. It's hard, but not the right kind of hard. The increased number of bosses (there are so many) only serves to make very few of them memorable or even remotely representative of the struggle that preceded them.
But you know, objectively, this is a good game. Never appreciated the Jersey-style murder mobs, but still a good amount of fun. The "Souls Game Feel" still belongs only to Dark Souls, I'd say. This game is just hard to be hard, not much else.

Why do I have to lose 10-20 minutes of my life if I make a single mistake? Moreover, you can be attacked while saving the game or using the terminal or rewiring box.
Second, the difficulty level is completely screwed up! In some places the game is completely unplayable even on Easy setting (don't call me lame, I play Dead Space nicely on Hard setting). Flashlight batteries that last only a few minutes? One-two revolver bullets or shotgun shells per box? Give me a break! The upgraded "cattle prod" doesn't even do any damage to the synthetics, as I remember in the original movie Lambert fried Ash with a single hit. The EMP bombs don't have any effect on synthetics - waste of time and resources. Medkits restore half of the health on easy level, wtf? The Joes always block your hits and beat the hell out of you in just 20 seconds. The human shooters are surprisingly good for an easy setting. Also being killed every few minutes and the constant need to play hide and seek with the alien or synthetics on easy difficulty setting really ruins the game. I had to deactivate the alien's and synthetics' AI to play through. Whoever designed the difficulty level should never get this job again!

Isolation successfully managed the one thing that every other Aliens game failed at since 1999, making the Alien a true and terrifying threat worthy of it's origin. And that is even not the only god-awful thing you'll be facing onboard the failing orbital station in your quest for survival.
The design feels genuine to the lore of the original movies, all from the design of the world itself but also the interface, the sound effects and the characters.
The suspense and horror unfortunately falls short halfway and after. Firstly how the Alien becomes easier and easier to ward off, becoming a nuisance rather than a menacing monster. Secondly how the story dragged on with too much filler between you and the climax, too many inconvenient failings to simply delay the plot too many times.
But in the end, they promised an Alien horror game, and they thankfully delivered.

I'm torn about whether to recommend this game. It delivered what I expect from a CoD: an over the top, fast-paced, preposterous story that was over in 5-7 hours (my play-time is inflated because I pause it while cooking dinner, etc). On the other hand, for half that time I didn't realize that it has a GPU memory leak that kills performance. I have a 980 Ti but was getting incredibly awful framerate by the 2nd or 3rd mission. The issue is not power--it's turning off the "fill GPU memory" option and then restarting your machine any time the GPU memory gets full. The game doesn't release textures correctly, so you end up with a GPU that is full and memory starved, and framerates hit single digits. Reboot, problem gone for 2-4 more missions. Rinse and repeat.
My recommendation of No is to send a signal to the devs that leaving this unfixed for 2 years is garbage. Glad I got a good price on this physical copy.

With beautiful visuals and great voice acting, Enslaved: Odyssey to the West is a hidden gem and definately worth its sale price. However I should warn that this game is buggy. Like real buggy.
Some areas of the map wouldn't load, I've fallen through the world quite a few times and the main character has a tendency to get stuck on random objects. One time the game crashed so hard it uninstalled itself from my steam library.
Even so the experience I had with the game was overall a positive experience and I would very much advise picking it up

Story - 8/10
The story was decent with some good moments and a good ending, though a quick ending. The story didn't hand hold you and explain every bit of the world but focused on the journey from the characters perspective.
Gameplay - 7/10
Really break down to 2 pieces.
The first is platformer - where it is as simple as seeing the next flashing object to jumo to. You can't jump to your death and you can not fall off of anything (Invisible walls). You are never going to die in the platform portion unless you are in a battle.
Second is fighting - This is where you can die. You are human and everything will try to kill you. The battle is good and you can increase your stats and abilitis as it goes on but you better like fighting as through the game it is fairly the same in the later sections.
There are also quick runs, where you are either chasing or running from something and have to beat the time clock to get it. There is no actual time clock but rather getting the object before it reaches X or running away so it does not reach you.
Camera was actually decent though if it forces you to look a certain way then it is because it is hand holding you to the next objective.
Graphics - 8/10
They did a great job of showing the world as it changed. Not much variance in colors but huge in structure types and vistas. They really stuck with RGB as primary and a spackling of yellow. Watch the trailer to see what I mean.
All in all a fun game to pass the time.

Playing this for the first time in 2017 made me realise how there are still such hidden gems around on Steam. Enslaved encompasses a simple yet addictive hack n slash combat system mixed with plenty of fun climbing scenes, set in a post apocalyptic world whilst telling a MINDBLOWING story  (especially the ending). WOW!
Enslaved has great believable and likeable characters whom show clear character deveopment with each having a clear skill set which is used throughout the story to work together to overcome bosses and so on. Having a heavy focus on story telling worked out great for this game and is really what made it the masterpiece that it is, however, there are A LOT of short cut scenes scattered throughout the entire game and I recognise that many players who want to jump / smash their way through the game will not appreciate... BUT... for those who see adventure games as an excellent way to tell a story as well as being immersed in the gaming culture it brings then this game is 100% for you!
I must admit, I am the type of gamer to usually stray away from these older titles, being a bit dubious of graphics, controls and so forth, however Enslaved has aged beautifully and shouldn't be judged by its release date. It should appeal to a broad  range of people and I am saddened I had not heard of this gem until recently recommended by a friend.
In short, if you enjoy action/adventure games with a great immersive story  and this game isn't in your library, then go purchase this right now!
