I bought this on sale expecting to play HW1 with better graphics and to have a copy of this game forever preserved on the cloud somewhere, even though I have the original CD. So far, things have been a huge disappointment. The following only applies to HW1 as I have not attempted to play HW2:
+ The graphics have indeed been modernized and fleet combat is spectacular to watch
- Every single ship has had their resource cost and battle prowess completely changed
- The AI of strike craft has been completely changed,  making fighters nearly useless in every type of battle
- Damage dealt by larger craft has been greatly increased, shortening combat and making tactical movement orders unnecessary
- Enemy fleet scaling has been completely changed, causing some missions to be stacked ludicrously against you and punishing you for playing well
The net result is that battles play out completely different. In HW1 Classic you had a framework for what to expect in combat: fighters would beat capital ships, capital ships would beat corvettes, and corvettes would beat fighters. Several craft would break these rules, but you always had the option through smart gameplay to even the odds - formations, tactics, and tactical movement could swing unfavorable fights in your favor. Now, in the Remastered version, all of that is pointless. Spend all your resources building as many of the biggest ships you can, and just drag a box around the enemy fleet to issue an attack order. Whichever side has the biggest fleet wins in a matter of seconds.
No thanks.
+ The classic HW1 game is included if you don't want to deal with any of this nonsense. Unfortunately, my experience with HW1 classic has been filled with bugs and crashes, something I do not experience when I install from the original CD

It's been a while since I've last played this, but god I love this game. I'm usually not a huge fan of first person shooters (I'm terrible and a lot of them seem to focus on being good at hitting and killing things quickly rather than a plot) but Borderlands 2 is super fun, amusing, and not so hard as to be impossible for those unskilled at FPS games. It was a bit confusing at first to me since I had not played the first game (I bought this when I only had a mac and therefore couldn't play the first one...) but after adjusting to the world and the basics of what was going on the plot remained rather easy to keep track of.
Suggestion for those who like plot and who are also terrible at FPS games like me: Do the sidequests. Not only are they amusing (I got a sarcastic talking ammo-absorbing shield from one) and give you some nice loot (read: the shield, along with some weird freaking guns and money for days), but you get more insights into the world of Pandora and Borderlands as a whole and you get XP. Those story missions you need to do to advance the story and that start out once you get them as typically hard difficulties? Do enough sidequests and you'll get leveled up enough where they're normal or even easy (and once or twice I'd get them down to trivial difficulties) which means more time to focus on plot and less time worrying about not dying constantly and losing your money. Of course, you'll probably end up dying during some of the sidequests on the way, but that's typically not quite as frustrating. Only downside to doing lots of sidequests is they do take up a significant amount of time, but I found it worth it. Plus I'm the type who likes to complete games fully or close to and the sidequests gave me lots of fun (and funny) stuff to learn about.

This is an amazing framework to build on for the future, the building and crafting systems are pretty solid.  But more importantly the movement system is amazing, I first realized there was more to movement in this game when I ran from the initial starting point to the first base you're led to.  It was dark, I didn't know how to activate the personal light (It's L I just hadn't tried it yet) and I ran headfirst into a tree.  Before I could strafe I had run into it, and then something strange happened, I seemed to run
the tree.
Well it was dark and I was being chased so I chalked it up to pre-alpha, new game, whatever.  But after I'd survived the night and had some time to play around with the game without being attacked, I realized that If I ran at vertical objects I could run up them a bit.  Tapping the jump button when I was close to an edge after running up a wall allowed me to grab the edge and pull myself up (You can also climb half walls by tapping jump next to them), it took some getting used to but after some practice I can scale two or three story buildings as long as there are handholds of some kind (windows, half walls).  Not to mention the wall running, which If I were the type to build a free-running obstacle course with the in-game building system (I'm not, but maybe if I get bored enough) I could probably waste another twenty or so hours on that alone.
Now I've played Mirror's Edge so I wasn't new to games with excellent movement, but I just wasn't expecting it in a pre-alpha game marketed as a building/survival type.
The building is pretty easy, and bit more detailed than most games in which you can build freely in an open world.  Foundations, walls, fortifications, ceilings  are your starting point, add half walls, doorways etc. to taste but if you build too big you'll need to use support beams to hold up your floor.  The added realism of needing proper support for larger buildings also plays a part in the 'destroy' part of the game, since you could bring down a significant portion of a building by attacking the foundation or beams.  There may not be anything currently implemented that powerful (Explosives, missiles, other high tech future stuff), but the potential is there.
Destroying things can be pretty satisfying, your building tool also doubles as a 'grabber' for wildlife and some enemies, and slinging the mouse in any direction will fling the offending object out of your way, and possibly into nearby rocks or trees.  If it's your kind of thing just walking around gobbling down rocks and trees for materials is a good way to waste an in-game day, if it isn't your thing you can change how fast you gather materials or how much material is recieved from each item destroyed.  Most nights you'll be holed up in base keeping your things from being destroyed, healing walls and turrets, or possibly just watching the carnage unfold from your personal observation deck if your defenses are good enough.
The enemies aren't too terribly smart, but their types reflect how they act.  Bug-types, swarm and overwhelm mostly, there are a couple other types, but nothing smart enough to get through a well-made defense.  There's a very Starship Troopers feel to defending your base sometimes, but nowhere near the sense of dread since the enemies mostly mill about the ground attacking your doors and getting chewed up by your turrets, there are some flying enemies, but if you keep your turrets upgraded they aren't too large a threat.  Having some enemies to scale walls and attack turrets or doors on the top of your base, or maybe some that could slip in through windows to attack power supplies.
Currently at what I assume is 'endgame' tech (fully upgraded eden kit, multiple level three turrets, two weapons with tons of ammo), surviving the night feels like being a lone Marine in a well defended base facing a really poorly timed zerg rush, I feel like if they all came at once I wouldn't stand much of a chance, but they're staggered enough that my turrets wipe them out in droves.
But there are certainly worse complaints to have about a pre-alpha game than 'It feels like Starship Troopers or Starcraft sans the Protoss but I'm not dying enough' so even if these guys go belly up tomorrow and this is what I'm left with to play I still consider it money well spent.

IMO this is the best game in the currently popular genre of alien planet/sci fi, open world/sandbox, crafting and combat games. We are told more of a storyline will follow.

The big bonus of this device is you can also pick up any living creature within the beam by holding down your mouse button, and hurl it to oblivion, if you don't have time, or want to switch to your kinectic shotgun to save the precious ammo. Currenty my distance record is clear across a lake!
The start is suitably challenging and you'll likely die a few times before you get your base defences up and running. I did.
There is an annoying but realistic liklihood that whilst your taking a rest and quenching your thirst via the inventory, some or deep in resource gathering, some alien beastie is likely biting into your ankle! You will lose health and suffer damage to your suit, also gain infections from such encounters.

Hopefully the devs will expand on this in the future, because for me this one currently plays the best. Would be nice say if the planet had a darker and hareder side for example.
On the whole highly recomended even in early access. The  devs are very responsive and enthusiastic too.

this game has such fantastic potential. It's mass effect meets mincraft meets skyrim meets day Z all in one. the developement team have lots of work still to do. there are glithes to be worked out , questions to be answered (both basic and in depth) and new pieces of the puzzle that should certainly be added, but the premise, game play, look/feel, and open world that Flix interactive has created here is truely one of a kind. I see eden star growing emensly in popularity in the coming months, especially as the developers continue to work out certain kinks and round out the game as a whole.
Positives:
-Concept...everybody in the gaming world loves Scifi and the world of Eden Star is reason enough why. pioneering on an unknown planet where you have to build, scavenge, and fight to survive is way cool.
-Look/Feel...the scenery is breathtaking.  the passive and agressive fauna and enemy hives are very original and beautiful.
-Game play...The interactivity of the world is very well thought out and makes for a very enjoyable in game experience. Mining, crafting, building, defending, upgrading and expanding all in order to stay alive and accomplish your goal makes this game real to life. a pioneer on a hostile planet in real life would face these exact same circumstances.
Negatives:
-Purpose... Not much info is given to the player following the opening cenimatic about who you are or why you are here on Pharus 7. the description of the mineral Teslinium states that it is the primary reason you have come to the planet, but no specifics as to why are given. not only this but after the initial opening cenimatic there are no further instructions, quest objectives, destinations or otherwise overarching goals to keep you motivated and enjoying the story of the game. the game is still in developepment so this is a bit to be expected, however this HAS to be finished. not having any purpose in a game like this will kill the excitement fast and the game will become pointless. after all the quest lines were finished in skyrim and other similar games everybody got bored really quickly so bethesday put out DLC's to keep the hype up, and it worked well for a while, but a well developed story with a detailed plot and coinciding quests and objectives OTHER THAN...stay alive, must be the drive behind any long lasting award winning game.
- Incomplete build and craft... there are several minerals in the game which can be found at specific spots only. these are most notably Tennal, cerilium, ironite, and uranium crystals. these minerals and a few other things seem to have little to no purpose in game. Old video's of gamers using these to build or craft can be found on youtube, but if you try to utilize these items in building your base they aren't even available in the most rece3nt versions of the game. perhaps I'm doing something wrong, and I just need a bit more instruction, but honestly I'm not sure what else to try. so far I can't find a purpose for these items. which brings me to my next point and it's a big one.
-Tutorial...there is virtually no tutorial whatsoever for this game. the menu screen has a button listed "how to Play" which takes the player to a web page with detailed instructions on most aspects of game play, but many pieces are left out. this is where an in game tutorial could and would shine. additionally the controls for this game are anything but intuitive. if your on a PC the controls are very frustrating and require alot of practice to master, even after doing so however the preset control sceme doesn't make sense. you have to jump from one end of the keyboard to the other regularly to play effectively and it makes things needlessly complicated. all this could be explained well in an in game tutorial while also dealing with other incomplete aspects of the game, i.e storyline.

TL;DR summary - An enjoyable game with gorgeous graphics and art design, some replayability (probably twice as the two different playable characters), and interesting plot. The recent updates have fixed the PC porting issues, and performance is good throughout (although some mild framerate drops when using the Temporal Device). 8/10
Pros:
- Great plot, which follows on from the previous games
- Good to be able to choose between Emily Kaldwin and Corvo Attano, with suitably different 'powers' for each = replay at least twice
- Sumptuous graphics and art design
- Great sound design
- Good level design: the developers provided multiple ways to complete missions (that reward players who like to find alternative solutions over the direct 'brute force' approach)
- Fun and useful 'void powers' for stealthy and overt playstyles = more playthrough opportunities again
- Your actions affect future events in the game to some extent
- Just long enough
- Good price reduction ATM, or bundled with the new expandalone: Death of the Outsider
Cons:

Very good, but not great. And for the record, I had no performance issues except for two random crashes, so this review is solely based on the gameplay.
I liked the first entry in the series but didn't really fall in love with it. It felt a little cold and rather short. For better or for worse, Dishonored 2 feels a lot like Dishonored 1, but in a bigger world. So I still like it but I don't love it. At least it's a longer game, but that has good points and some bad points too.
First, the bad: Along with this bigger world also comes many more convoluted character names and places. There are so many names to keep track of it feels like a bad mob film. As a result, the narrated story unfortunately feels force fed, relying so heavily on *telling* what's going on rather than letting the player discover what's going on.
Then, the good: Story aside, the choice system feels good. You can hack and slash your way through the game, or sneak quietly through, or do some combination depending on the situation. That said, I think the plot feels more satisfying if you sneak more than you fight. In most levels you can also achieve optional tasks to complete a mission but all seem to sway on the less lethal side of things.
And the very good: Quicksaves are extremely welcome! Hit F5 to quicksave, and F9 to reload. If this game was checkpoint only, I probably would've stopped playing on the first level.
And, finally, the merely OK: The available player upgrades offer some useful perks as you progress, but nothing feels like a must-have item. Later in the game, searching every room for coins and jewelry to gain money when there's not a lot to spend it on just feels like a waste of time.

The Souls series are games about endurance, not skill.  It's always been like that and it's not different this time around with Dark Souls 2, the best one up untill now. Dark Souls 2 is a dark fantasy, adventure with rpg elements.
As an avid rpg lover, this has made me play NONSTOP from release, barely trying many other games out. I may take a break now and then as I did when playing WoW, but never a break over a week, it truly is addicting because of its massive amount of items and playstyles available, always making me come back for more especially after its predecessor.
Story - The story is not quite as good as the first game, but serves the gameplay. The main problem I have with the story is the final boss and ending cutscene, feeling not quite fleshed out and simply telling you nothing much else is going to happen after. This may change with the 3rd dlc I hope.
- 8/10
Graphics - The environment is amazing, but not quite interconnected as its predecessor was.
The quality of the weapons, armour and spells are definitely some of the best looking out of most rpgs, although many of the bosses and enemies you cannot get their weapon and/or armour, you usually have an item very similar in looks to these missing items (except the old dragonslayer).
It could do with a bit more variation in beast or demon-like monsters, but has very well thought out enemy design.
- 9/10
Audio - The audio is quite displaced in a lot of areas, however where it is placed correctly, will give you the ability to percieve where the next enemies or traps will be. Very defined sounds such as torches and the occasional arrow or two will let you simply see by feeling where it came from.
The mirror knight pre-patch had a certain attack which the sound is bugged, being able to hear it even if your sound was on 0 ingame.
- 6/10
Gameplay - This is arguably what makes the souls series of games, with big expectations because of its predecessors.
First off, powerstanced weapons feel very weak with the biggest trade-off being stamina, when weapons two-handed will provide the same damage with less stamina, bigger poise-breaking and ultra/great weapon class's ability to not be parried gives them almost no utility. There are certain weapons that rise above however, such as dual rapiers, great hammers, straight swords and the specialized weapon such as the Warped Sword or the Majestic Greatsword.
I did feel as though a lot of weapon classes such as maces, dual wield axes, great axes, claws, dual wield halberds and ESPECIALLY reapers have very boring movesets (both axes and greataxes not so much, but could do with more imagination still). Dual wield with all of these weapons also in account, they simply need to be more worthy in combat by simply having more reach, speed and differing movesets than how they are currently, there's a reason almost no one uses these weapons outside of "cosplay" (dressing as a character from the series or other series etc.).
There is a BIG problem to do with animations in PvP, with the enemy standing still on your screen, yet hitting you.
There is also weird bug/implementation to do with poise, if you hit someone at the end of their dodge roll, they will take the damage yet not be staggered in any way, which they then will use to their advantage to backstab you. On the subject of poise, some weapons such as katanas seem to stagger you quite often, no matter how much poise you have.
Certain enemies seem to have very weird AI. One such being the fire salamanders. which will lock onto your character and never lose sight of you while propelling fireballs making it very hard to combat them even when you're right in their face. The salamander will propel fireballs which have a 1-3 second delay not even giving you time to run/heal.
Outside of these problems however, is the best experience in PvP you can find through challenge and tactics based gameplay using spacing and environment knowledge, weapon knowledge, prediction and using items to your advantage.
- 8/10
Community - The community is very split, with 50% being people who will "gank" (multiple people fighting one person), hack and be generally nasty towards other players.
The other 50% are the kind ones who will see you using just your bare fists (no vanq seal or caestus)/ladle/broken weapon and join in using the same items. There are also the players who "cosplay" and those who will help you with fight against a gank (with one of us being summoned and the other invading) or those who kill a ganking host with a lifedrain patch, which is just beautiful.
- 7/10
Overall, a 8/10 (This is reviewed before the final dlc release which may change my opinion on the title)

I really really wanted to like this game, had it since release, have checked it out every now and then.
But it's simply garbage.... Been streamlined to hell to cater to a larger audiance, which destroyed the essence on which the title thrived in it's previous games.
Next too that, the game only becomes decent IF next to having spent 60 bucks on basically a broken game on release, you pay an other 100 bucks to gain all DLC.
I somewhat like the improvements on the campaign map, but hate it at the same time. You can't even build wooden walls for your smaller settlements. On the other hand, your forced to specialize towns, which gives them all their own stratigic value, something that was missing in previous Total War games.
AI is horrible, and I mean a step backwards from Shogun's AI, as in, will walk into 3 units of phalanx head on never attempt to flank bad....
O did I mention Phalanxes where broke on release and could be slaughtered by peasants ? Yes heavily armored troops, some of the heaviest in the world and amongst the most discplined, could be slaughtered by peasants....
Battles feel rushed and because units break like crazy, grand tactics are out of the window, it's all about bring heavier units then your enemy.
In fact, it's become more of a economy simulator (and before they patched the building tree's a horrible on at that).
And after 2 years, all they done is stream line the game some more and add back functions we had in every total war game, like fire at will and hold ground (yes you are reading this right, that was NOT added in release).
I've only gotten around to write my review now because i'm so utterly sickend by the game for which I was waiting forever.
If they updated the orginal Romes graphics and released that for 60 bucks I would have been more satisfied.
Even the basic path finding on the campaign map is broke. If you move a army that would be faster embarking into ships and then sailing over and landing, prepare for the path finding to screw up and take your army 4 additional turns over land.
And then there is unit collision, which wasn't there in Release, which basically lead to major mosh pits, when battle where at the time won by formations and discpline. It was just a laugh. Now they have fixed it by forcing units to stay in formation and everything, but it's obvious it's not something the actual engine itself does. So basically the game is running on a engine that is not suited for the game at all. Yet ever since Empire they stubornly hold onto this engine, and with Shogun they got away with it because they polished it so well you didn't notice it. But F me Creative, get the hint already! Either update your engine to support it or pick a better suited engine!
We want our realistic like combat, Total War is picked because of that, if we want Arcade combat, we have a 100 games that do a better job then Total War will, stop trying to cater to people who shouldn't be touching this game to begin with, all you do is drive away the people who do love these types of games.

I am calling this the Excitebike of today! It is really fun with the career mode and the depth of control you have over the rider, plus it has its own dirt physics! The only problem I see so far is that the AI is fairly easy, so I may have to ramp it up to a harder difficulty.

Before I say why I recommend the game, I'd like to put forth a few caveats. First of all, even on the highest setting with Pro physics, the AI isn't too hard to beat, and this is coming from someone born the same year Mount Everest was first successfully climbed. The AI appears to have enough straightaway speed but the human player seems to be able to negotiate the corners better. It's not a deal breaker for people like me, but for the very skilled, well, you're going to be bored against the AI, but then that's why there's online racing.
To be clear, it's the overall speed of the AI which people might find not as challenging as they wish. In all other respects, the AI riders are outstanding. They take different lines through the corners. They battle one another and occasionally they fall over or crash. They will react to a human player or another AI driver by moving over or sometimes changing lines to block. And they ride differently from one another as they race, they don't all run some hypothetical best racing line. They do seem very much like human racers.
If you do want more of a challenge, race in first person view rather than third person or chase view. You will need a video card that can handle it and probably a strong stomach as well, as this can be a bit nausea inducing. It does make the racing more difficult, but at a  cost, so I can't really say that it's a viable solution for everyone.
I'd also mention that I've never raced motocross, and it's been four decades since I've been on a motorcycle. So I cannot address the realism of the representation of motocross racing versus the real thing from an actual rider's point of view. However, I think this is true for most people playing a racing game. Also, realistically there's no point in trying to sell again that's so realistic that it would be impossible for most people to play it with any level of accomplishment.
My thumbs up recommendation is based upon my perception as I play MXGP. It
like what I would imagine a motocross bike would feel like to race. I'm using an Xbox360 controller on my PC and controlling the bike is smooth and intuitive. I race with Pro physics and using the two sticks for steering, bike tilt and body lean, I have no issues at all.
In my opinion, a successful racing game should present the player with a risk/reward challenge. MXGP does this well. It's possible (again, using Pro Physics) to drive easily and stay upright and on course. However, by judicious pushing at the right time, the player can be rewarded with a lower lap time, although he or she risks a tumble if pushing just a bit too much, or if an AI or human opponent gets involved. This is what a proper racing game should do, give the player a sense of satisfaction for taking risks.
Additionally, the tracks in MXGP don't force the player into a "best" racing line. It's possible to try different paths in corners, over jumps and even on straights, trying to tie together a better lap. Again, as a player, it's my perception that I'm going faster because I'm exploring difference approaches to each section of the track, and that's enjoyable. The tracks have realistic looking ruts, humps and bumps and during my races I felt that those track features made a real difference to my racing success or failure.
The tracks in MXGP present an interesting variety of layouts, elevations and difficulties. I find the variety challenging and again, enjoyable. Graphically they look pretty good as well. The graphics are not 2014 cutting edge, but I think cutting edge is a waste in a racing game outside of the track itself. It's good to have trackside objects to give of speed and provide a sense of  immersion for the player, but objects that are too complex a polygon count would raise the minimum and recommended specs for the game for no real additional purpose. It's better for more folks to enjoy the game at 60 fps. This is not to say that the trackside objects are sparse or of poor visual quality. The opposite is actually true, there are plenty of things to see and they give a great visual appeal to the venue where you are racing.
The  lack of a challenge from the AI mentioned at the beginning is really the only serious complaint I have, and of course there's always online racing if you want more of a challenge. I've done several online races and it's pretty straightforward to find a race. I did experience a lot of lag of the other players' avatars, but probably most of them are on the other side of the Atlantic from me, so that's to be expected. The game did run smoothly even with the other racers' lag and with the collision option set to off it really didn't affect my enjoyment.
So overall I'm giving this game a positive recommendation. I would strongly suggest that anyone who might be interested in purchasing the game first give the demo a try. The demo is very representative of the experience you'll find in the game.
Thanks for reading this review!

Coming from a pretty seasoned MX Sim & MX VS ATV player & experienced MX rider I thought I'd give my 2 cents.
PRO's:
Real sponsors & bikes.
Real tracks.
Real riders.
Track deformation.
Cornering feels great. Sliding it into a tight turn and powering out feels better than any other mx game out there.
Throttle control. Again, using throttle control to kick the back end out is wonderful.
First person actually looks & feels good.
Actually needing to brake.
The game looks nice...just about. Bike models look amazing, well done.
Pretty in depth career mode, & 1st one for a long time.
Customisation of the bike settings before a race is great.
Practice/Qualifying formats.
And finally well done Milestone for a simultaneous PC release!
CON's
Physics in the air feel awful & clunky.
Ready Steady Go start format? Is this Mario Kart? Should just drop the gate & the clutch...(see next point).
Theres no clutch!!??? Massive negative here.....
Why can't I control the whip/scrub? Don't animate such an important feature!! Doesn't feel fluid or natural.
Track deformation doesn't make a difference to handling.
Ruts and berms don't feel supportive & I feel like cross rutting isn't an issue, even late in a race.
Spin outs and wheelies can feel random at times.
No rev sound on the start gate & in the air?? Get that stuff recorded and implement it!! Basic stuff there...
Rear brake & panic rev doesn't do much in the air.
Why make 250F's unable to clear most jumps? They're pretty much as fast as a 450F irl, sometimes out qualifying them.
Summary.
To be fair, on the ground at least MXGP feels great. Cornering is good, feedback feels great, the rider positioning and animations are spot on and you can make this engine look good once you have got it down. But the clunky whip/scrub feature and the lack of rev sounds brings you literally crashing back down to earth with a bang.
The career mode is deep and rewarding, although I get the impression a few things could have been pushed a little more. I guess not being able to choose which clothing brand I wear is due to clothing being tied to some teams & manufacturers with it being official sponsors and all. But it just feels like some design choices could have been implemented a little better.
I love mx games, and will buy them regardless to support the industry. We need developers to keep making these games so it pushes them further. If Milestone release an MXGP 2, or MXGP 2015 or whatever its called, I think it will be great, but this one just falls short of a great title.

Dishonored 2 is an action-adventure stealth video game developed by Arkane Studios and published by Bethesda Softworks. The sequel to 2012's Dishonored, the game was released for Microsoft Windows, PlayStation 4, and Xbox One on 11 November 2016.
The game takes place in the fictional city of Karnaca. After Empress Emily Kaldwin is deposed by the witch Delilah Copperspoon, the player may choose between playing as either Emily or her Royal Protector and father Corvo Attano as they attempt to reclaim the throne. Both Emily and Corvo employ their own array of supernatural abilities, though the player can alternatively decide to forfeit these abilities altogether. There is a multitude of ways to complete missions, from stealth to purposeful violent conflict, navigated through a sandbox environment.
Ideas for Dishonored 2 began while developing the downloadable content of its predecessor, which spawned the decision to create a voice for Corvo Attano after being a silent character in the first installment. The advancement of the timeline was brought about once Emily Kaldwin, only a child in Dishonored, was first proposed as a playable character. The game's aesthetic was influenced by paintings and sculptures. Set in the new fictional city of Karnaca, its history was invented over the course of one year. The city itself was based on southern European countries like Greece, Italy, and Spain, drawing on the architecture, fashion, and technologies of 1851.
Dishonored 2 was released to a positive reception. Praised were the improvements made since the first game: the more challenging stealth, the adaptability of Emily and Corvo's abilities to both play styles, the art direction, the creative design of individual missions, the realization of the game's world as well as the replay-value and the artificial intelligence. Criticism was directed at the lack of focus of the overarching narrative. Aside from this, technical blunders as well as issues with the PC version were received unfavorably. Dishonored 2 won the award for Best Action/Adventure Game at The Game Awards 2016 and for Costume Design at the 2017 NAVGTR Awards.

One of the most anticipated games for me. Dishonored 1 ranks easily on the top 5 games i have ever played. And here i am, finally playing Dishonored 2 almost a whole year after its release. After about 40 hours i am closing in to finishing my first playthrough, playing with Corvo. Yea I am the kind of guy that wont proceed until i have opened every drawer and every cupboard possible, and will replay the mission if a body has been found. I enjoy this game so much, that i try to make the experience last as long as possible .
A worthy predecessor of Dishonored 1 (D1 in short). The story is very well made. It has followed a different route than D1 . I dont feel as if they have recycled the same things from D1 , making the experience of D2 feel as if i was playing a Dishonored game for the first time. I have found the plot very intriguing and interesting and some parts of the game have left me astonished
. There are many different aproaches on each mission and sidemission so you can shoose according to your prefference. And remember, allways pay attention to the smallest details and clues when playing ;)
The gameplay has improved providing more options throught the 2 available charachters.
Corvo and Emily and their unique Outsider powers , allow the player to fit the playstyle to his liking (either going all-in and slaughtering every person that crosses your road, or going stealthy AF ) .
The level design is extremely well made, providing dozens of different aproaches on each mission and different ways and paths to move/explore the area around you.
The artstyle..... I cant say enough about the artstyle. It follows the D1 distinctive kind of steam punk  - cartoonish art style that made me fall in love with D1. Music and sound are amazing making you ''live'' rather than just play the game.
Regarding game engine and performance issues, playing D2 with a 3rd gen i5, 8gb of ram and a gtx1060, i havent noticed any problems and have constant smooth 60fps on high-ultra preset.
Will definitely do at least two more playthroughs. Will try a different charachter and a different aproach each time . Note that both Emily and Corvo powers and rune / bonecharm progress save and are available in NG+ :)

The game creates a very tense mood and atmosphere, as good as the movies, even better on some parts. The gameplay is smooth and the game is very optimized. The only thing keeping me from giving it 10/10 is that after 10-15 hours, it feels very dragged on and the objectives feel repetitive to the point of being annoying, by the end of the game I just wanted to finish and the alien(s) didnt even scare me anymore.

Who is this game for: I know a lot of reviews will say this is a horror game, and while not wrong I think it is more accurate to say this is a hunting game where you play as the prey. So this game is meant for those who want expieriences when they play games, because that is what this is, an expierience.
The game has next to no glitches that I ran into, really cool aesthetics, soundtrack is fitting, AI is pretty neat, and the game definitely can make you feel like you are in the original alien movie which is cool too.
Who is this game not for: This game is not for impatient people, or people who have a hard time projecting themselves into/roleplaying a game. If you look at the alien and treat him as an npc then yes, you will find this game incredibly boring. Boiling the game down to its mechanics and ignoring the environment and world that has been setup for you will destroy any of the good things this game has going for it.
If you played similar games (like amnesia or penumbra) and didnt like it I would still recommend giving this a go. The game isnt downright scary and it never really does much to make you scared but it does a whole lot to make you tense and afraid. As someone else on the internet once put very poetically (though I will contort very uneliquotentially for my purposes),
"Alien Isolation is a game about Potential. Remember that word, Potential. Potential is great because its something that allows you to watch tv or browse the internet all day without cashing any of it in. Potential is wasted energy. Sure you could cash it all in at once and see what comes of it, but then your moment is gone."
That is what I feel like this game conveys to the player, sometimes its better to be resting on your laurels because of the potential you have.

Multiplayer seems like it would be very rewarding as having fellow colonists to harvest resources and upkeep the base would make it easier to keep your outposts and make attacks against hives.
A good feature of Eden Star is that you can adjust the world settings (such as player damage %, structure damage %, structure hit points, thirst & hunger depletion, enemy spawn rates etc.) and use Free Build mode if you want so that you can focus on base-building without having to repair anything or worry about dying. It's an enjoyable game so far and I'm looking forward to seeing the dev team add more to it! ****

I believe this game is for a certain type of player. First if you are impatient this game is not for you. If you crave constant action then you probably won't like this. If you don't want to spend any money then this is not for you. If you like to hunt, enjoy the reward of patiently stalking and killing something, have some money to spend; then you will probably like this.
I'll comment first about the gameplay then about the pricing of the "free to play" in the second/third paragraph.
The game has a slower pace to it, I'll give an example of a typical hunt for me. I spawn at a lodge and load up my equipment in my inventory; I'm hunting whitetail and maybe turkey today so I want my shotgun for versatility and bow for stealth, I could take my .243 rifle but I prefer the shotgun. It's early in the morning and I can see the misty dew settling on the grass plains. The air feels fresh as I slowly wander about looking for my sign. A red tracker mark over some footprints point me in the way of a deer and I walk after it. I want to rush and sprint but I must be patient lest I spook it away. Droppings indicate to me how far it might be, more footprints help me close in on it when I hear the grunt of a buck. I crouch down and sit. I could stalk it down, but I'd rather the deer come to me. I pull out my deer call and mimic the sound of a doe to the open air. A call from the buck responds in kind. The bucks grunts get louder and louder, I know which way he's coming from but there is too much brush in the way. I lay down amongst some grass to make my profile even smaller and wait for him to reveal himself. At last I spot him standing tall and he calls out for the doe in my trap. He is still too far out so I maneuver onto a small hill for a better vantage while he gently and slowly walks in. I watch him closely and load a shell of buckshot into my shotgun, he suspects nothing. He has a decent set of antlers, nothing special, but he carries himself as a king. Still, I know my role as assassin well and wait for him to close in  enough to see the grain of his antlers. Finally he stops before me and raises his head high as I hold my breath to steady the shot. Silence tells him nothing until a cacophonous blast reverberates through the air and scares away any nearby animals from the king as he falls to his knees and lands his face in the dirt. I pull out my huntermate, snap a trophy shot, and claim my work. Walking away I eject the spent shell and load another, there's plenty out there yet on the reserve today.
The game looks pretty good and I can tell they put quite a bit of work into the environment. There are a few bugs that happen in multiplayer but otherwise the game itself is very good.
Now for the reveal of the abnormal market. Since this appears to be a niche game, they have decided to get it paid for in a way, I think, most steam gamers aren't accustomed to. The free-to-play isn't, its more of a demo really. When you first start out you can only hunt mule dear and rabbit with your one .243 rifle, and shooting rabbit with your rifle will give you disqualifying kills. If you want to hunt everything then you can get, at minimum, a 10$ membership which is good for 3 months. On top of that you'll want calls, other weapons, equipment, which all cost real money.
To further the currency explaination: The game has paid for currency (em$) and earned currency (gm$). Em$ is a cent to cent ratio, 100em$ is $1.00. Almost every weapon is 4-6 dollars, yeah, I know. Each call is over a dollar, clothes costs a few bucks (don't buy individually, get bundles), stands, blinds, other items are all going to be 4 dollars or so. In other words, you can easily spend more than a triple-A $60 title. In other words, if you put money down, spend smart (research stuff) and make sure you're getting what you want.
Gm$ are earned by doing missions and are terribly underutilized and overpriced in the store. I do enjoy doing the missions, a little extra goal and challenge to a hunt, not too hard to accomplish. With gm$ you can buy one single shot shotgun for 6200 (I have it, I like it) otherwise you can get sprays to attract animals or bait and that is pretty much it. You would think at least some clothing but nope. You can get animal licenses individually with gm$ but its priced so high for a beginner its not worth it (1800 gm$ for 1 day of turkey hunting). I sort of understand why everything is so expensive compared to other games but I don't agree with it.
A little more about my experience that may be helpful. I hunted with a friend who picked up items so I didn't have to get everything, he got a bunch of mallard gear, I got a bunch of geese gear. I only hunt with the .243 rifle (given for free) which is good for most deer and coyote and fox. A 12 gauge shotgun, which can shoot anything except birds with slugs and birdshot can shoot those (you get three kinds of shells and it replenishes for every trip). So yes, with one shotgun you can shoot any animal in the game, given somewhat limited range. Finally a compound bow which is great for stealth and when you have multiple animals coming as it won't scatter them like a gun. So my method is very up close and personal usually but only took the purchase of the bow; the pump-action shotgun came with a membership bundle. If you want to hunt big game with a rifle get something up in the .300 caliber range and you're good to go.
So as a result: Good game for patient gamers who have decent income. Bad game for someone looking for an actual free-to-play game like War Thunder or LoL and/or doesn't like somewhat realistic hunting. Of course you can always try it out yourself. Do the tutorials when you start it up (Hunt Now -> Tutorials) Also read up on the wiki
has a lot of useful information. If you do decide to get into the game and put down money. I recommend one of the membership bundles, you get a lot more than getting it individually.
If this review isn't helpful please comment why and I'll do my best to improve it with what you need to know.

This is by far the best puzze/action game I have played in a long time, possibly ever, however be forewarned that although the game is a complete arc of a story, the ending is quite unsatisfying and the full story will likely never be actually told due to poor sales and an over-inflated budget on initial release.
So enslaved hits all the usual notes once expects from this sort of game; solid brawler combat with ranged options, jumping/environment puzzles, hidden collectables, skills and equipment that you gain as the game goes on, a levelling/power up system etc.
The difference between this and most games of the genre is that all the above things are done well. The Combat is nothing new, but rock solid with tight controls and a variety of combos with the standard light, heavy dodge-roll etc moves. the environments are ♥♥♥♥ing stunning, and only outdone by the character animations which due to motion-capture are fantastic. Voice acting is one of the best I have ever seen in a video game, and character development and expression on par if not better than many oscar winning films in the last few years, and the story, although yet-another-journey-to-the-west re-interpritation is actually done very well.
Overall a must-get for fans of the genre and highly reccomended for anyone who even considers playing action games, unless you're an absolute sucker for a completed storyline, in which case, avoid as this one will sadly never be concluded.

Enslaved: Odyssey to the West is an absolute hidden gem from the previous consol generation.
Reminiscent of some of the best action advenure games available, such as Uncharted and Tomb Raider.
The plot is an adaptation of the Chinese novel 'A Journey To The West' but set in a near future distopian world, were you attempt to return a resourceful, yet lost girl, to her homeland.
The story drew me in immediately with a fantastic opening sequence and a beautifully well realised world.
The port to PC is a pretty standard affair but it controls well and benefits from an uncapped framerate and 21:9 support.
Combat and traversal are also engaging and good enemy variety presents a reasonable challenge.
If you're a fan of action adventure or Ninja Theory's work, Enslaved comes highly recommended.

If you have no knowledge of motocross or Euro style motocross then I wouldn't reccomend it. Coming from a seasoned American MX guy the game is great at touching the FIM series. The phsycis could use some touching up and so can the body control but the concept of the game is great.

While more of a simcade than anything, MXGP is a must own for any MX fans out there. While far from perfect, MXGP tries to aim for a slightly more realistic approach to MX racing via realistic cornering and braking physics, but falls short with poor jumping physics and poor bike sounds. A CONTROLLER IS HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!
Pros:
+ 14 Real world tracks to choose from
+ Realistic cornering and braking
+ Authentic racing experience (Real tracks, bikes, teams and riders)
+ Good graphics
+ Bike tuning (though somewhat limited in terms of options) actually affects the way bikes behave
+ Decent AI (15 AI riders supported in offline play)
+ Intense multiplayer races see players banging bars as they fight for the perfect lines (12 players supported)
+ Mo-capped rider animations look awesome
+ Realistic helmet cam view (if that's your kind of thing)
Cons:
- Horrible bike sounds (what is this, Excitebike?)
- Poor jumping physics (lack of mid-air control/no gas gyro effects)
- Scrubbing seems rather mechanical and automated (players are only required to push both sticks in the same direction near the lip/takeoff of a jump which requires no real skill and uses the same animation over and over)
- Track deformation is mostly cosmetic (players cannot physically ride in ruts formed on the track)
[*edit* after 5+ laps, corners are harder to take due to braking ruts/bumps forming, however bikes ride 'on top' of the dirt as opposed to 'in it' thus resulting in mounds forming in corners as opposed to ruts which players can ride in for better traction.]
- Relatively steep price (although not gameplay related)
Still highly recommend picking this game up as it breathes fresh air into the MX racing genre, providing countless hours of fun on tracks which are easy to learn but hard to master (and pays off if you do). The game has good AI for those who wish to play offline, but online play is where this game truly shines. Despite the games efforts of providing an authentic MXGP experience, a track editor would have been a nice touch.
TL;DR
Great MX game which is a step in the right direction, with room for improvement. If/when improved, could easily be one of the best MX racing games out there.  8/10

Bought during the Steam sale this summer. "Pre-Alpha." Yeah okay. It's telling both of the skill of this team, and the slipping bar of the rest of the industry, that you'll quickly forget this thing is supposed to barely be running. It's aleady engaging, challenging, and just fun. Be prepared to lose some time. Might want to set an alarm.
I have encountered precisely one glitch so far; a respawn pad, when on a foundation that's clipped into the ground a bit, may respawn you under the world. In about 5 hours of gameplay, that's all. That's 5 hours in a pre-alpha release, folks.
What gets me most excited about this title is that there appears to be a solid technical foundation as the first priority. What's implemented tends to just work. This means that as they go forward and build momentum, they can add *content* and not enter the "we released too soon" death-spiral of bughunting and mechanic-fixing. They seem to have their priorities straight. They're extremely up-front with the state of the game, the content on offer, the use of the Pre-Alpha designation, and parts of their roadmap. This is what Early Access is supposed to be for.
But hey, maybe we can't all afford to buy everything on principle just because we support the idea. So did I mention it's a blast? Never did such a clueless person who could barely remember the controls have so much fun blindly running for his life from I'm-not-even-sure-what in the dark because he foolishly strayed too far from his piddly base at night.
Finding mats, food, water, making ammo and upgrading weapons - feels like I wish Fallout 4 Survival mode did.
I've RLF from an area because I was out of bullets, occasionally stopping to fling a pursuer who got too close into orbit.
I've spent the night huddled in a sealed bunker listening to Things destroying my last auto-turret because I didn't pay attention to the mats needed, or how to make the repair tool, or that i was low on lead - wondering if they were going to breach the walls.
Even after getting past the "okay maybe I'll go read the damn guide now" phase, it's still challening and engaging. How far will you stray from your base each day? How many days will you go before realizing you really ought to be hunting those nests down? (You'll see.)
On top of all that, I coulda sworn his name wasn't there an hour ago but Gareth Coker is now listed on their site as Composer - he who made the Ori and the Blind Forest soundtrack. Only good things will be happening.
The dev's openness and transparency are a large part of why I chose to jump in with Early Access. I hope I can contribute in some way, but I'm liking where things are going, it's already fun to spend time in, and I feel like no matter where things go from here, I'll have easily gotten my money's worth - and I get to see an amazing ambitious project develop around my virtual eyes.

Based on first impressions and the price, you might think this is one of those knock-off brand games that is poorly optimized and designed. It just needs to do a better job of emphasizing its strengths. It is a good game, far better than expected. It plays like a typical third-person action platformer (similar to God of War I think).
Looking around with the mouse is not great, it plays much better with a controller. Besides that the action is smooth, responsive, and still enjoyable (I'm at chapter 9 rn). Platforming is easy and you don't really have to worry about messing up.
In terms of visual/audio, it's very strong considering the price of the game (I guess this would be a AA game). The scenery is very beautiful, and the atmosphere/world building is nice. Options menu has basic graphics options like resolution and low/mid/high/ graphics. Resolution could be better in the game, some of the texture work is weak, but I've only noticed it once or twice. Audio quality is good, nothing special there.
Story-wise, there are a couple issues, but nothing that prevents you from enjoying the game. The first sets of levels feel artificial, in that you are just going from one crumpled building full of mech to the next. That changes soon enough and the level design expands and gets much more creative. One very noticable flaw in the game is that you often need to knock over a thing in order to cross a gap or whatever. It's just way too convenient that there is always the exact thing you need hanging above the gap.
All-in-all I recommend the game if you enjoy action platformers, especially if it's on sale. I started playing it just to kill half an hour this morning and ended up playing for six hours straight. The only serious flaw I see in the game is that so far there has been only one path to take for nearly every platforming section. It's a very linear game, which is fine, but definitely doesn't lend itself to multiple playthroughs. Oh and you can't change the button layout.. cmon guys it's 2017.
tldr; not quite as polished as AAA titles of the same genre, but plays well, looks fantastic, and is genuinely enjoyable.

"Papers, please.", the name of this game is also that one piece of dialogue you will read over and over and over again. You are an inspector for a communist regime, in a fictional country set in 1982. It is your job to keep the country safe, now that its borders have opened up again (a little). Natives and foreigners alike will have to show you their papers, including passports, ID cards and permits of various sorts and you must check them for credibility. Basically, Papers, Please is a simulation of the actual job of a border guard. Since this is set in a dystopian, cold war-era though, it is far from boring. Security is tight and you cannot afford any mistakes, especially because the life of your own family depends on it. After each day of sieving through papers, you will have to spend your hard-earned salary on rent, food and warmth for your loved ones. This forces you to work fast, though working fast makes you more prone to errors, which in turn might lead to penalties for any mistakes, even those as small as forgetting to check the date of expiration on a worker's permit.
Putting yourself and your family first will mean absolute obedience to your regime, however, and a strict and methological approach to every single one of the (partly random, partly story-related) visitors. Some will tell you sad stories about how much they miss their family, others will flat-out lie to you and it is always up to you if they may enter or not. A psychological experiment, one could say. Will you stand up against a cold government and turn a blind eye on those with no malicious intend or will you be absolutely loyal in order to secure your paycheck for the day?
Playing through the storymode will confront you with various events, setting off chains and affecting the game later on. Apart from this, there are also some endless-gamemodes included, such as endurance (work until you run out of money) or time-trial (finish up as many people as possible within a given time).
Papers, Please is one of the most interesting games out there right now and it does not even need any graphical miracles to pull that off. In fact, the monotone, pixelated world only contributes to its disturbingly grim atmosphere.
What would you do?

I find this game pretty interesting. You play as a documents inspector working at a border checkpoint. Oh yeah, this is a checkpoint that leads into a corrupt, dystopian, and fascist nation.
The game goes out of its way every so often to test your sense of right and wrong. Will you let a woman who lacks documentation but is in need of an experimental surgery that is only available in your country past the checkpoint? Or will you deny her entry in order to retain the job you need to provide for your family?
Gameplay is pretty much just examining people's passports, permits, work passes, etc. and then issuing a stamp of denial or entry. Curveballs get thrown at you though which mix up the variables that ultimately decide whether a person can pass or not. And with about twenty endings, the game knows how to keep you engaged.

Broforce has you take the role of a random 80's action hero parody as you shoot and blow up lots of stuff while trying to rescue fellow hero's and make it to the exit in this 2-D side scrolling platformer shooter.
The barebones plot is basically there as a joke to Action movies of the 80's and the America ♥♥♥♥ Yeah additude of that era.  Your shooting terrorists for freedom and america.  Thats it.  Its very tounge in cheek and since its barely there it won't get in the way of the gameplay.
The game handles very similarly to super meat boy but with lots of shooting and explosions.   You can shoot through nearly every surface of the game allowing for some intresting ways of tackling levels.  Enemies will kill you in a single hit and there can be a lot of them so its a nice balance between tatical and reflex gaming.
The most intresting mechanic is the Bros themselves.  You start off as a rambo clone with a machine gun, greanades, and one life but its not long before you find a POW and upon saving them you switch to a new unlocked Bro with different weapons and a different playstyle and you get an extra life.  Every time you save a POW or die you switch to a random Bro and every few POWs you save unlocks a new Bro.  This will constantly force you to change up your tactics and you'll want to keep playing to see the next movie parody Bro unlocked.
Outside of Unlocking Bros There are an intresting variety of enemies and hazords and some really cool boss fights to keep you entertained as well as online drop in drop out co-op play.  The campain itself will last you 5-7 hours and it lets you play from the start with all you unlocked Bros which adds to the replay value.
My only gripes are that the jumping is very floaty which lead to a lot of cheap deaths and that some Bros are way more useful then others.  You'll scream when your trying to past a wave of bullets and the game keeps giving you melee characters when all you want is a gun.
Overall the game is simple and fun with lots of colorful characters and a very aware sense of humor.  Ideal to pick up and play for a couple of hours at a time.

NO SPOILERS AHEAD:
A worthy sequel to dishonored which expands upon and adds to an already brilliant gameplay experience in an engrossing world with rich history ,mythology and intriguing characters.
The new items and powers that are introduced are overall a massive improvement to the first game ,giving the player the ability to approach combat and stealth in new and exciting ways even for veterans of the series. The crafting system is also quite good and adds to the experience rather than being the annoyance i expected it to be. Level design is on par with it's predecessor for the most part and better in quite a few instances.
Combat and stealth can be challenging but overall are relatively easy even on the highest difficulty settings. If you are a newcomer to the series it might be a decent challenge.
While the voice acting delivery is quite good ,the writing is atrocious with the story being definitely one of the weakest points of the game lacking in originality ,variety and urgency.
Beware of lengthy load times and performance issues which unfortunately still plague this game. On 1080p with a gtx 1070 oc and an i5 4690k @ 4.5ghz i had to turn down water details ,shadow quality and environmental detail to very high from ultra as well as disable bloodfly and rat shadows for a mostly constant 60 fps (which on rare occasions would momentarily dip to as low as 30fps!). Considering my pc can run the witcher 3 wild hunt maxed out with hair works on and a huge ammount of graphics enhancing mods at 60 fps this is hardly the performance you would expect from a game with such mediocre graphics.
While the graphics have definitely seen a massive improvement ,distant lod looks horrid even on ultra ,shadows have a tendency to flicker and texture pop-in is extremely apparent even on an ssd.
The in game sound is also bugged and probably not performing as intended. Instead of giving an idea about the location of an enemy it renders the player all the more confused. For example: you will hear footsteps beside you while the enemy's location might be ten metres below you and conversations will linger in your ears unrealistically when you have left an area.
Overall it is an excellent game well worth your time but unfortunately in it's current state is not worth the asking price. A must buy on a sale.

The first few minutes are going to kill this game if something is not done about it. I'm all for being dropped into the middle of a situation with no chance of survival, its fun. But in this game you are (Presumably a colonist who will have gone through training to get there) dropped in with no idea how the little equipment you have even works while being mobbed by aliens that plausably explode on death (Nice touch by the way) If you stick with it and get passed an intro that by all rights can only be appriciated by the developers and total moasacists then you are faced with a pretty standard survival game of today played on hardcore mode. Permadeath is something I love and switch on in every games its available.  The problem is that here its not all that needed once you have a little experience of how to build a defence system or nine. After that surviving the night just becomes a matter of waiting till the guns go quiet and then picking up anything useful you find among the enemies dead and checking to see what was damaged in the attack.
I want to recommend this game because it really has some interesting features, and using a zero point glove to hurl enemies off a cliff never gets old, but the game is just too shallow and had the whole rinse and repeat of defend, repair, craft and attack about it and nothing else. This game needs either something is the area of a story to follow or some target other than survive the next attack. Being alone on an alien world gets old is all I'm saying.

After playing the game all week while being able to work with John from FLIX [due to Work Experience and an awesome bunch of people at the University and College near me], my overall impression of Eden Star is "Throughly Enjoyable with hours of replayability with friends".
While the game is still in Pre-Alpha and with new patches being rolled out this week [26/05/2017] it does sometimes that feel that the game can become akin to a grindfest [Although that is most Sandbox games] due to a lack of features in its current state, BUT while playing with friends [and filling an entire sever] Eden Star becomes a lot more enjoyable since colonys add a whole other layer to the gameplay;
By this I mean:
- Strategic Base Building
- Arms Race from Spawn [Similar to the Nuclear Arms Race until you reach a stalemate]
- Base Raiding with/against your friends [The salt smelled like the League community]
While only three points cannot fully express how fun multiplayer can be while playing with friends I do recommend playing it if you can stomach the few issues with multiplayer which are;
- High Ping while connected to your regional server [This is because the ping counter takes into account lag aswell as ping]
- Random spikes of desync
- Glitches when battaling other players [Such as no damage and one-shots, less than 25% occureance but still annoying]

I don't even know where to begin to do proper justice in praising this game.  At first glance, it looked to me like any other puzzle platformer hack'n'slash. Having grown up on Legend of Zelda and Prince of Persia, I love that kind of thing, so I thought I would give it a try.  I got it on sale for $5, but I wouldn't consider it overpriced at $20.
The gameplay is fairly straightforward with mostly linear maps; you are very unlikely to get lost.  The combat is mostly simple (with a few twists during boss fights that make you think a little bit) but very satisfying, with excellent combat animation.  The combat and platform puzzles are enjoyable, but not the reason this game is a hidden jewel.  What really make this game great are the little details, the breathtaking visuals, and the lifelike performances that make the game come alive.
The two lead characters, Monkey and Tripitaka (Trip) are voiced by Andy Serkis and Lindsey Shaw.  They both provided motion capture, so their characters' motions and facial expressions are grippingly real.  The relationship they develop over the course of the game is powerful and believable, and where I generally hate having a companion forced on me in a game (they almost always feel in-the-way), these characters work together so well.  I found myself terrified of failing Trip (and consequently dying), especially when first confronting a Dog.  Her AI worked for me and never felt intrusive while I fought mechs as Monkey, and their teamwork made their relationship seem more profound.
All sorts of little details made this game come alive for me.  The way Monkey often has to catch his breath after a mech fight makes him feel more like a person than an action hero.  Trip is often terrified - of the mechs, of the constant threat of death - but pushes herself forward with the hope of reuniting with her people.  The scenery, especially during the early game set in a post-apocalyptic NYC - not dead and brown and rusty but overgrown, green and vibrant - was spectacular.
Not everyone will love this game the way I do.  It is not very long and could be finished in about 10 hours, give or take a few based on personal skill, difficulty level, and how much you explore for collectibles.  The maps are linear, which some people don't care for.  The combat can feel repetitive, especially if you mash your basic attack on easy difficulty.  The ending seems to be hit or miss for most people.
But if you could appreciate believable characters with strong chemistry, beautiful scenery and a strong, compelling story, consider giving it a shot.  If you happen to see it on sale for the price of a latte, it is absolutley worth it.

This game undid the damage of Colonial Marines. It treats the Alien francise right. The atmosphere, the sound, the characters, the story. It all feels like Alien, and it all feels right. It doesn't feel like a random fan service, it feels like, well, an Alien game that belongs to be canon, among the movies. Well, atleast the first and second one.
The gameplay is great. The horror survival aspect works great, and the items and mechanics help it stand out as a unique game, not just ripping of other horror games, like Amnesia. And, crap, is it scary. Many horror games will scare me, until I figure out how to survive, then the scares slow and I feel more relaxed playing them. Not here, the scares never stop. (I won't spoil it, but the Alien isn't the only scary entity!)
The visuals are fantastic. Probably the prettiest space game I've played. I loved just stopping and looking at the game. The fire looks awesome, the dark hallways are terrifying, the smoke looks fantastic, it all just looks good. And it's optimized as crap, too! It runs fantastically! (Note: Some people have problems with it crashing. I've only had it crash once, but it should be noted regardless.) Outside the station looks great, I loved looking out the windows and seeing other parts of the station, or a nearby planet, all with shiny effects that look nice. Inside the station looks awesome, too! I love how instead of trying to look futuristic, it tried to look how the Alien movies look. It works fantastically, it feels like you're in an Alien movie.
The sound design is right up there with the visuals. All the original Alien things sound just like they did in the movie. And it's atmospheric as crap, I love walking down a hallway and hearing all the beeps and boops from the station, then in the distance hearing the Alien come out of a vent. Terrifying.
(No story spoilers ahead, don't worry) The story is top-notch! (Although I'm not as picky when it comes to stories.) It kept me wanting to play each night, just to see what would happen to the characters and how I would escape! The characters are great, all have their own personalities. You always know a game/movie has good characters when you constantly hate someone one, then seconds later can relate to them. It makes them feel real, and not as black and white. The "twist" at the end was fantastic, really loved it.
But that's not to say the game doesn't have problems. As I mentioned above, some have had a lot of problems with it crashing. There are a lot of weird graphic bugs. Remember how I would look out the windows? Sometimes the station will be there, sometimes it won't. Sometimes the planet would be there, sometimes it wouldn't. It's really weird. The sound, as amazing as it is, also has problems. When I move with a weapon, sometimes the weapon will make sound. I'm not sure if it's supposed to make that sound or not, it's so inconsistant it's hard to tell. Somes sounds just won't end up playing. (Like a fire will be completely silent sometimes, but sound fine other times.)
Overall, it's an amazing game, one of the best I've played all year. It has it's quirks, but it was nothing game-breaking. (For me.) If Colonial Marines funded this game, than it's disaster was worth it.

This goes on for a while until you find the *SPOILERS, AGAIN* nest of eggs, and it boosts back up and stays that way until the end.

So much promise, so much work, so much beauty and style, and yet: So much frustration.
If faithfully capturing and recreating the first Alien movie's look and feel were enough to make a good game, this game would be no less than fantastic. Sadly, a game and a compelling story need more than that - interesting characters worth caring about, and six letters: PACING.
The formula "activate X, oh no, access to X is blocked by Y, you need to get a Z to get there, oh♥♥♥♥♥♥ the Z is supposed to be in the A, but someone took it to B and to get there you need to get rid of C" is compelling once or twice, but if the whole game consists of setbacks, it gets old and tedious. The same can be said for a Ripley crashing through the floor and losing progress / being diverted: For god's sakes, it can be done once, or twice, but do it more often and players become incredibly fatigued about something that is supposed to be HORROR.
About the gadgets: I very much liked the idea of plasma torches and Security Access Tuners. but to have actually three levels of them just becomes repetitive, as well as having to re-start generators and all that - all of the stuff looks great, but simply is used to often. Why? I don't know, perhaps to give the game some additional length? I honestly prefer playing a three-hour game that has my interest for the whole three hours, than having to push myself through a seven-hour-deal of repetition with little variety.
The worst thing however is this: A game that is so unforgiving for every little mistake should either auto-save on every corner or GIVE PLAYERS THE ABILITY TO SAVE ANYWHERE, ANYTIME. Yes, I understand that the concept of manual Quicksave is alien (hah) on console games, and their progresskeeping mechanics swap over to PC games as well nowadays, and yes I understand the argument that it would break the sense of risk and fear. But I really can't afford having to repeat 20 minutes of gameplay again and again just because there is no save point between here and there.
It simply all adds to the frustation with this game which could have been so much, but all the beauty it offers is swallowed up by all the repetition you have to suffer through for various reasons.
If you love the original Alien film like I do, this game is a must-play.

HOWEVER, the game is still amazingly fun and deep once you get into it (git gud ya scrubs) especially the DLC zones, which feel a lot more akin to the level design of  "Dark Souls 1" and have challenging new mobs and Bosses.
In short, I'd say about 8/10 without the DLCs and 8.5/10 with them, if you like action RPGs and have the patience required to force through the first hours in which you will die, a lot , I'd really recommend getting it.

I find this game pretty interesting. You play as a documents inspector working at a border checkpoint. Oh yeah, this is a checkpoint that leads into a corrupt, dystopian, and fascist nation.
The game goes out of its way every so often to test your sense of right and wrong. Will you let a woman who lacks documentation but is in need of an experimental surgery that is only available in your country past the checkpoint? Or will you deny her entry in order to retain the job you need to provide for your family?
Gameplay is pretty much just examining people's passports, permits, work passes, etc. and then issuing a stamp of denial or entry. Curveballs get thrown at you though which mix up the variables that ultimately decide whether a person can pass or not. And with about twenty endings, the game knows how to keep you engaged.

Definitely a thumbs up and maybe even more, a reference in the genre.
If you like Setllers and its chain of production, behold, this gets to the next level and the flexibility of the game is incredible.
Start with your hands, dig a bit of ressources, assemble them and start automating tasks after task.
Your map will slowly grow in a huge automated factory that you could watch for hours if only the resources were infinite, but nope... Everything you build will probably need to be reconfigured as other sources are needed or as your production steps up.
If you like the challenge, you'll compete against a quite aggressive species on the world that do not like at all the nasty fumes that come out of your big mess.
Turrets, more supplies and research become necessary.
One mistake ? Your base could be wiped out by the swarm that tries to break your wall now and then. Plan with caution, avoid cutting the electricity if you decided to electrify your base.
Build tanks or buggies or exoskeletons and explore the infinite world until you find more resources.
Relocation there or should you build a fast train that will crush the once peaceful aliens ?
Mor automation, circuits, traffic lights.
Keep researching until you can build the rocket and go back to space. Meanwhile, the aliens will gather, grow and surround you.
Call for help and let them join your game cause your brain will not be sufficient alone.
Fluids, conveyor belts, rails, chests, cranes, roads.
This game is just awesome and its replayability is almost infinite because there is always room for improvement in your designs and the mods that the community provide can add more depths or difficulty to the production chain or the aliens.
A must buy, honestly.

You start out by creating a rider (personal data,appearance,number etc) then you are giving a wild card ride to choose on an MX2 machine, this happens for the first 2 races choosing between the lower level teams. LAST GEN technology

I initially bought this game when emperor edition was released in hope to avoid any buggy problems, and upon changing the prefrences.txt file to direct x 9 the game did look good and worked well.
However thats where the praise ends, even when pushing through the games initial early rush with the harder factions on vh I get to a point were I no longer want to play were I dont feel any need to play unlike previous TW games. In my opinion there is no flavour to this game, unit/building cards offer no actual value, they may as well be an excel spreadsheet. This boring aspect is compounded by the lack of any connection with your generals, they are as replaceable as miltia units in previous games. They tend to die just as I learn their name and offer minimal diversity upon recruitment. Which is essentially what the game is, minimal diversity, it is so shallow upon not even completing the first chapter one could get 80% of the main army forces recruitment capability and as for economy as previoulsy mentioned it is a series of numbers taking into account a lot of other numbers with a red stamp. There seems to be nothing left to chance or the environment and no impact of chance within the things that matter for a Total "War" game.  Furthemore battle difficulty does not scale properly with ai units getting hugh morale boosts , as barbarians this actually makes it easier and more enjoable to autoresolve any likely victory in the early game  due to their comparative lower morale. Futhermore public order and taxes have been sidelined with population gone altogether, what replaces it is growth and minimal building spaces, this restrictive nature means the player has to trade off between competing uses though in reality land in this age is not scarce and buildings only require research not sufficient population or city walls.
Battles themselve lack any feeling of impending doom and make for a boring 10 minutes, this I feel is where it strikes out, the game could of been based around battles and conquest it seems instead to be an interconnected series of dots on a map with autoresolve, which in my opinion is far too much of a grind
In campaign on normal ai behaviour is stupid, on hard they are too leniant and do not seize advantages and on very hard they are good and smart but have overwhelming money and get a full stack in three turns. There is no defaqto ai in which the game is enjoyable. I want a valiant victory over the enemy not to fight replenish, fight replenish, fight replenish until siege.
The positive:
- nice differences in battle diversity
- military alliance ai works very well
- campaign map looks good
- boats work

The negative:
- complete lack of connection in all aspects of gampelay
- Rome does not come knocking on the players wall
- Card are terrible
- Inferior game mechanics
- Very limited zoom in campaign and battle map
- Unit cards are indistinguishable in battle
- Battles are too short
- Limited building spaces are artifiical
- Political system is a chore
- No historical events
- lack of diveristy between generals and no legacy
- boring number crunching
- events are dumb
- hand held missions and objectives, I do not need to be told to attack a trespassing army
- Nearly all armies are full stack
- Campaign map does not change
I find myself wanting to love this game but just cant
