I am not really here to say how awesome the game is, but it is. A lot of people have had issues with AMD graphics and performance issues related to RAM and HDDs. I have 8 GB of RAM. All it did was warn me that I was low on memory and reccommended closing other programs, which I did. I bought this game naively thinking that my card met the minimum requirements, and according to some benchmarks, it doesn't. I have not had any issues with performance. Due to all of the negative comments, I was really worried that I would need to take a lot of time tweaking things on my computer and possibly even upgrade hardware. This wasn't the case, my below-minimum AMD graphics ran this game just fine. I haven't tried it on anything about the most lenient of graphics settings, but the game runs fine, and for me that is what counts. I don't have an SSD, and it loads fine. Maybe other people should look into clearing space or defragging? As far as memory, just make sure you close background programs. I installed Razer Cortex to help with it, but it's really not even needed for me.
In short, this game ran fine straight out of the box, I didn't have any issues. I'm probably going to turn my graphics settings up too, it runs so well.
For reference, this is my hardware.
Intel i7-6700k Skylake 4 GHz
MSI AMD Radeon R9 380 4GB DDR5
8GB DDR4 at the lowest speed I could find (I'm cheap)
Cheapest Terabyte HDD I could get my hands on, mostly free of files
Nothing is overclocked.
All of my worries were for nothing, the game runs fine so far in my limited minutes of playing it.
Now, after playing the game through once, I will give some more details. If you are a guy who falls into habit of doing things repetitively, this game is repetitive. You need to learn to switch things up. If you always attack a base with a rocket launcher, next time use an APC with some allies in it. Don't always attack with a helicopter, you'll get bored. This is somewhat hard for me because I would rather do things the fast way, and don't have too much imagination for doing things differently. I'm sure that can be improved though.
The main character is nearly invulnerable, but later bases and missions will be quite challenging, though he respawns with full ammunition not too far away. If you want a challenge, this game might not be a good idea for you.
The Land, Air, and Sea DLCs are pretty overpowered on top of that, making it even harder to get killed and easier to blow stuff up. Again, if you are up for a challenge, don't get those DLCs. They go beyond OP.
The other smaller DLCs are okay I suppose, I have a few of them, and with the exception of the Reaper Missile Mech, they aren't overpowered at all. I don't really use them though, they're just sort of a repeat of what we already have in the game. It mostly just gives you a head start, and in my case, a head start on capturing bases repetitively.

Homeworld is a space RTS game released in 1999, it gained popularity by not only creating the single most intuitive space strategy mechanic to date, but also had an amazing story line and one of the most beautiful music scores ever. In Homeworld and Homeworld 2, resource management is key, every resource you collect on one mission gets transferred to your next, so it is a good idea to use it wisely, often relying on salvage ships to steal enemy ships over building your own. Space combat is done on a fully 3D plane, where ships can easily move in all 3 axis, which at the time was revolutionary.
Gearbox did an amazing job in remastering this great gem, the graphics is amazing, while keeping the story and the music intact the game is truly perfect now. They made some UI and control changes but in the end it results in a smoother gameplay.
There are a few minor bugs such as a sound issue with ship engines when too many of them are moving at once, and the tutorial being slightly broken (you get asked to press okay to continue to the next segment but the tutorial continues on as if you already pressed it), however these are minor gripes and does nothing to ruin this wonderful title.
My ratings are as follows:
Graphics 8
Music 10
Story 10
Gameplay 9

I've owned this game since launch and a lot of the bugs have been ironed out. There are still some there though. Gearbox did a lot right with this and it's a fantastic title for those looking for nostalgia. With the UI updates, the Remastered version plays like a 2015 game, making it playable for a wide audience.

I highly recommend this title.

I've just finished Dishonored 2 for my 1st time and I feel like I have to contribute by writing a review.
+: I really liked that there are more stealth powers to acquire, as previous game was almost forcing me to kill people, considering the powers I was given (but I finished it in low chaos tho), but in Dishonored 2 there are more interesting ways for stealth. For example, here right from the 1st mission the guards are all in positions where it is not easy to take them out unnoticed, however in Dishonored 1 I just knocked down everybody easily and could run across the halls. It doesn't work here and I love it, the game challenges you more, especially when you play without powers. I might try it sometime, because I feel I wouldn't survive without Blink and Bend Time (especially in the last missions).
What's good too is that missions are more different from each other than in the last game, sometimes gameplay changed a whole lot (in the 7th mission, for example, I really suggest you playing that mission). And again, there are a lot of tricky ways in order to get runes and bonecharms and to complete missions as well. Oh, and the new Void is much better. Overseers here are also more developed and it is great that they don't seem now as a bunch of crazy religious people as they seemed in the last game.
-: I'd say the main downside for me in this game was that I had to wait about 8 month to play this game. Welp I preordered it and I was sure I can play it, because even though my old laptop was... old, the minimum requirements were met. Anyway, even at the minimum visuals I couldn't play it, fps dropped to 10 or 5 so I decided to play it once I get a new laptop. Now that I've got it I'm not that amazed by visuals, I have no clue why the game was so demanding in this case.
I liked the plot how it began, but as it followed it was quite disappointing. In previous Dishonored the story was like a rollercoaster, you could never tell what's going to be next and you were so excited. Here, there are far fewer surprises for you and the ending is like (I played on low chaos) oh you didn't kill anyone so here you are a great ending for you, and everyone lived happy the end. I hoped for something unexpectable, really, but the whole thing was basically just about one woman from Dishonored 1 DLCs. Nothing so special.
In any case, I recommend playing this game because it is interesting and wonderful. My rating would be 8/10
That's everything for now. I may edit my review as I play more or get some new ideas.

This game will mostly appeal to fans of 8-bit designs and twin-stick shooters, as it's a well-made game fusing those two things. The game is colorful and loud, with frantic twin-stick, top-down shooter controls (i.e. left stick moves your squad around with aiming/ shooting taking place via where right stick is aimed.) Fans of retro chiptune style music will find some enjoyment from this soundtrack, as hefty explosions fill the rooms from the various weapons you throw out to annihilate the enemies including screen-filling grenades and various missiles and turrets.
What bothers me about this game the most is that it seems like you are more often a victim of friendly fire and exploding barrels more than the minimal attacks from enemies, making for a somewhat clumsy feeling level of player interactivity. I think this is somewhat intentional with the game, however.. as you seem to be making a mad dash through the levels to complete the various objectives before a timer/"radiation" begins to automatically do damage per second to your party until they are dead if you take too long to complete the objectives, which some players may find annoying to be racing against a clock to complete the levels and not able to explore freely.
The game could use more boss or objective variety, with objectives ranging from pushing puck-like objects into incinerators on the map or eliminating all enemies, but the main gameplay of running from room to room and eliminating the enemies is fun. The gear you can buy your characters seems pointless and very limited to just a few helmets / hats that don't seem to affect their stats or weapons at all and are cosmetic-only(?). You may end up unlocking more gear as your characters level up, but I'm not certain as I haven't had any characters live for very long.
I got this game on sale and enjoy 8-bit design aesthetics, and enjoy booting it up now and again to try to progress through a few levels and see how long I can have my guys live for. I'm uncertain if there is an end-game or if it's endless levels, but it's fun to boot up and mash through a few stages with its frequent explosions and enjoyable chiptune soundtrack. I think 9.99 for its default asking price is a bit high, and would feel better about snagging it under a 5$ pricepoint.

The music is great, controls are responsive, and I like the randomly generated ships. I feel like it is a little bit expensive for the content though, so I would wait for a sale if you are interested.

The second main thing to worry about is falling, and while there seems to be no apparent fall damage, you do however take a minor, itty-bitty, bite sized fatality from falling off the edge. Oh, did I forget to mention the edge? Yes, yes of course I did, as I so dutifully lacked at mentioning, the setting is also placed in an Avatar like sky dimension. And no, unlike avatar, there is no way to get down to the joyful, barbaric blue-monkey people waiting for you down below. In fact, on the note of down below, there also seems to be NO down below, and absolutely no way to get to this nowhere. So, enjoy 20$ of sky-running and trying not to get molested by small insect-like buggers that are keen on literally coming out of every known terrestrial orifice known to man. All in all, a great game. Impossible, but fun to play. Unless you're me. Then, in your attempt to pull off a sweet parkour jump trick, you literally die before the tutorial even kicks in.

I'm really jazzed about this game. It's already got so much stuff, and it's still in Early Access, so I can probably look forward to even more.
It's one of the few games that I've watched the video, thought "That looks awesome," and had the game live up to the expectation.
So what is it? Well, the campaign is pretty short - really more of an extended tutorial, so I'll talk about the Free Play. It's kind of survivalish, in that you start as a dude with a pickaxe on an alien world with hostile fauna. From there, you build up your mega-factory-complex-of-awesome by building increasinly complex stuff from 6 base resources (copper, iron, oil, coal, wood, water). And automation is the foundation layer of the game. So you can have automated mines pulling ore from the ground, which then gets loaded into an automated train, which hauls it to your automated smelting center, which feeds your automated factory complex. It's beautiful.
This game is one of my favorites and I'd highly recommend it.

I've spent a considerable amount of time with this game, both modded and unmodded and I wanted desperately to love it. You don't always get what you want. I did get the game as a gift from a friend though, and our desperation to love the game enough to play together led to many a wasted hour trying to find happiness.
This game may be summed up in one word – Shallow
The strategic map has more in common with Settlers of Catan than Risk. The cities are nothing more than a series of slots you can put buildings into that provide a flat military, public order and/or economic boost. 6 per major city, no more, as has been the case since Empire. There is never any sort of feeling of progression or accomplishment that comes from building the finest city in the world and this is due in no small part to how terrible the AI is at handling the strategic layer.
The AI will march with its armies in the 'double time' stance virtually everywhere, literally forcing you to ambush them in order to engage as ambushes are automatic when attacking an army in this stance. You will never see properly developed cities anywhere that you haven't built yourself as the AI is also incapable of even feeding itself by building enough farms.
The diplomacy is also a joke on normal - wherein everyone wants to be your friend no matter what and your borders simply are never threatened - and virtually every other faction conspires against you on any setting higher than normal. I had some small Spanish tribe declare war on my Seleucids because of how I treated the Persians. It never makes sense, and even modded it is still a complete pile of♥♥♥♥♥♥
The fleets thrown against you, if you can call them that, consist of the lightest, cheapest, smallest possible ships which are incapable of posing any real threat. The armies are made of 10 slingers and 10 hoplites if you're fighting against the Greeks and 10 spearmen and 10 slingers if you're fighting against anyone else. That is not a joke or hyperbole. The AI never constructs the proper buildings to field good armies even when they have the technology to do so. Enjoy seeing a lot of really advanced artillery along side sack-wearing peasants forming the army core. It got so bad they had to 'rebalance' the building chains. All this did was add military units to the city center to hide the fact the AI is such a ♥♥♥♥ing joke that after more than a year it still couldn't/can't build a decent settlement.
When it comes time to actually play the battles you're in for your biggest disappointment yet, as they are by far the worst of any total war game. Remember Spider Man climbing your walls in Empire? Imagine the Human Torch at the gates of Rome... Throwing torches. Even now, after countless patches, even modded, the battles suck. They are terrible. I have never witnessed the AI do anything other than stretch its forces into the longest line possible and simply march toward you. No skirmishing - the ranged units merely stop and fire at you when in range until the melee have made contact. No holding the melee back to inflict casualties, nope, they just keep going forward until they route. Every battle. Never holding any units as reserves. Nothing but march forward and die.
Unless, of course you are playing a defensive siege battle. Those will make you wonder how the hell they thought this game was even finished. If you're defending all you need to do is put units in front of the gates and at the stairwells leading up to the wall. If the enemy takes the wall or breaches the gate they simply run on in and get slaughtered. They won’t flank around off the wall, they will simply walk down the stairs, one at a time, until the unit routes and you win. And that's if you're lucky and the AI actually used its siege equipment. More often than not it will simply run its army forward to throw burning torches at the main gates, one unit at a time, until the towers of your city have routed them all. If they actually do manage to get through the gates, the entire enemy army will attempt to enter simultaneously and all die due to the burning oil poured down from the gatehouse.
Things get far, far worse if there is more than a single army being commanded by the AI in a battle. Take the above example of the entire army rushing through one gate and add a second army, which started on the other side of your city, which will march around your city, as close to the walls as possible suffering horrific losses, just to charge into the same gate. No flanking, no tactics, nothing but a sad disappointment, which is exactly what this game turned out to be.
Oh, and the naval battles are the same as the land battles. No differences what so ever in tactics needed to win or those used by the AI.
TL:DR – Game is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ reskin of Fall of the Samurai.

I was first introduced to smite mid 2014, my first experience with a moba. My friends were already at a much higher level than myself and I got stomped. I thought, "it's not for me," and moved on.
November last year I was invited to try again and since it had been a while I thought things might've changed, they hadn't, abuse was thrown at me and it became the first game where I had rage quit after being told to leave by team mates. This left me feeling bad.
I eventually got back into the game around February after I bought the founders pack for Paladins which gave a skin for Ares. I redeemed the skin and decided to create a new account.
I re-did the tutorials, worked my way up, understood the gods and how to work effectively before I switched back to my actual account. I'm not the best player at my level but I'm not exactly the worst, my win:lose is about 1:1 which is how I like it.
The game controls well, looks decent and has some good music and sound effects.
